items.titleZh: 降低 GPU 系统中的高带宽闪存延迟（佐治亚理工学院、英伟达、斯坦福大学）
items.descriptionZh:
佐治亚理工学院、NVIDIA Research 与斯坦福大学的研究人员发表了题为《SlipStream: Enabling HBF for GPU Systems by Mitigating the Latency and SRAM Overheads》的论文，探讨如何在GPU系统中更有效地利用高带宽闪存（High-Bandwidth Flash，HBF）来支撑大语言模型推理。随着LLM规模和批处理规模持续增长，推理系统对内存容量的需求迅速上升，传统HBM虽然在带宽和延迟方面优势明显，但受限于DRAM密度和成本，难以单独满足更大模型、更长上下文和更高吞吐的需求。HBF的核心思路是用NAND闪存替代HBM中的DRAM晶粒，并沿用HBM式的高带宽接口，从而以闪存的高密度和成本优势显著扩展GPU系统的内存容量。

不过，HBF要将NAND闪存引入GPU内存层级，必须解决两个关键问题：一是NAND闪存的访问延迟显著高于DRAM，直接暴露给GPU计算单元会拖累推理性能；二是为掩盖延迟而引入的缓存、缓冲和调度机制会占用宝贵的片上SRAM资源，影响GPU原有计算和缓存效率。针对这些挑战，论文提出SlipStream机制，目标是在GPU系统中缓解HBF的延迟和SRAM开销，使HBF能够作为大容量内存层级的一部分参与LLM推理，而不是仅停留在理论容量优势上。其创新重点在于面向HBF的延迟隐藏与数据流管理，减少对片上SRAM的过度依赖，让GPU在访问大容量闪存时仍能保持较高的计算效率。

由于新闻摘要未披露具体性能参数和对比数据，目前可确认的是，该工作由上述三家机构合作完成，并明确聚焦HBF在GPU系统中的可用性问题。其技术影响在于：如果能够有效降低HBF延迟和SRAM开销，GPU系统将有望突破HBM容量瓶颈，以更高容量支持更大参数模型、更大推理批处理以及更长上下文窗口，同时改善推理服务器的内存成本和扩展性。应用场景包括大模型推理部署、长上下文服务、高吞吐批处理推理以及内存容量受限的数据中心GPU平台。总体来看，SlipStream并非简单替换内存介质，而是通过系统级延迟缓解和片上资源优化，为HBF进入GPU内存体系、服务LLM推理提供了关键技术路径。

items.content: Jensen Huang’s stunning resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Now prominent figures are calling for Huang’s reinstatement, and many are also hopping on board with a theory spreading throughout Silicon Valley: that the scandal is the result of a plot against the former CEO.At the center of this theory is the reporting from The New York Times that former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, one of multiple women Huang is accused of having an affair with, is a Chinese spy. US agencies haven’t confirmed whether this is the case, and President Donald Trump claims he was unaware of any spy allegations. Jensen Huang’s alleged relationship with Alice Huang set off the events that led to his resignation; subsequent reporting suggested he had an affair with two employees at Nvidia, including one of his direct reports. The revelation raised new questions around whether Nvidia customers, including Megaspeed, were funneling chips to China in circumvention of export restrictions. Last year, Nvidia intervened in a chip-smuggling probe surrounding the Singapore-based company, according to Bloomberg.David Sacks, a venture capitalist and former White House AI crypto advisor, has made it clear that he’s skeptical about The New York Times’ reporting. In a post on X, Sacks points to an article from CNN, which says US officials still can’t confirm that Alice Huang was a spy. “The spy narrative is collapsing already,” Sacks writes. He continued to question the spy allegations during Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event on Monday, saying: “The reason why Jensen lost his job is because of this lurid Chinese spy allegation. So if no one’s willing to back that up now, then again, I question why this entire chain of events happened.”Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney similarly expressed concern about how Huang’s resignation played out. In a reply to Sacks’ post about the CNN article, Sweeney said, “What?! So journalists with sketchy motives portrayed rumors from god-knows-who (lobbyists?) as facts sourced from intelligence officials and gaslit the NVIDIA board to push out the founder, CEO, and once-in-generation visionary?” Amjad Masad, the CEO of the AI app and website builder Replit, called the timing of Huang’s resignation “suspicious,” adding that “if Jensen, the premier champion of open models, is taken out then anyone who wants AI closed, centralized, and controlled might benefit.”SemiAnalysis, a research and consulting firm for the semiconductor and AI industry, posted a “conspiracy theory take on the situation,” speculating that Huang’s removal is a way to “remove opposition to an extremely hawkish China export control bill,” referring to the Remote Access Security Act (RASA). The bill, which Huang opposed, would extend AI export controls to cloud servers that allow companies in restricted countries to rent access to Nvidia’s AI chips. The Department of Commerce released an interim final rule on Monday in an attempt to address this loophole.RelatedThe Nvidia scandal isn’t slowing downWhat could China get from Jensen Huang?More than 185,000 people, including Sweeney, Masad, Elon Musk, Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, and Shopify CEO Tobias Lütke, have signed a “Stand with Jensen” letter, calling for his reinstatement as CEO. The letter similarly calls for a closer look into the circumstances surrounding Huang’s resignation. “We have not been shown evidence substantiating the allegation that the woman at the center of this controversy was a spy,” the letter says. “Suspicion or association alone is not a sufficient basis for ending Jensen’s leadership. The inquiry must establish the facts, not merely justify an outcome already imposed.”

items.titleZh: 科技领袖们确信，黄仁勋的退出是一场针对他的阴谋。
items.descriptionZh:
据英文报道，英伟达创始人兼CEO黄仁勋在执掌公司33年多后突然辞职，震动科技行业。随后，多位知名人士公开呼吁其复职，硅谷还流传一种阴谋论：这起丑闻可能是针对黄仁勋的策划。争议核心是《纽约时报》报道称，前Megaspeed高管Alice Huang——黄仁勋被指与之有婚外情的多名女性之一——是中国间谍。美国机构尚未确认该说法，美国总统特朗普称不知悉任何间谍指控。报道称，黄仁勋与Alice Huang的关系引发了导致其辞职的事件；后续报道称他还与两名英伟达员工有婚外情，其中一人是其直接下属。此事还引发新疑问：包括Megaspeed在内的英伟达客户是否规避出口限制，将芯片流向中国。彭博社称，去年英伟达曾干预围绕这家新加坡公司的芯片走私调查。

在技术政策层面，争议与AI芯片出口管制漏洞相关。半导体与AI行业研究咨询机构SemiAnalysis提出一种“阴谋论解读”：黄仁勋被移除，是为了“消除对一项极其鹰派的对华出口管制法案的反对”，即《远程访问安全法案》（RASA）。黄仁勋反对该法案。RASA拟将AI出口管制扩展到云服务器，使受限国家企业无法通过租用云上英伟达AI芯片算力来绕过实体芯片出口限制；美国商务部周一发布临时最终规则，试图堵住这一云访问漏洞。换言之，政策焦点从“芯片是否跨境”扩展到“算力是否可远程租用”，影响AI训练和推理算力的跨境服务模式。

业界反应方面，风险投资人、前白宫AI与加密顾问David Sacks对《纽约时报》报道表示怀疑，引用CNN称美国官员仍无法确认Alice Huang是间谍，并称“间谍叙事正在崩塌”。在Semafor活动上，他质疑整条事件链：如果无人愿意支持该指控，为何会发生这一切。Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney批评有动机不纯的记者把来源不明的传闻包装成情报官员提供的事实，并“煤气灯”英伟达董事会，赶走创始人、CEO和一代 visionary。Replit CEO Amjad Masad称辞职时机“可疑”，并认为若开放模型的主要倡导者被移除，希望AI封闭、集中和控制的人可能受益。

请愿方面，包括Sweeney、Masad、Elon Musk、Uber联合创始人Travis Kalanick、Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan和Shopify CEO Tobias Lütke在内，已有超过18.5万人签署“Stand with Jensen”公开信，呼吁恢复其CEO职务，并要求彻查辞职相关情况。信中说，未看到证据证实争议中心女性是间谍的指控；仅凭怀疑或关联不足以结束黄仁勋的领导；调查必须确立事实，而不是为已经强加的结果辩护。整体看，该事件已从高管丑闻演变为涉及公司治理、AI芯片出口管制、云算力监管以及开放与封闭AI路线之争的行业性争议。

items.title: China retains fastest supercomputer in the world crown as AI data centers soak up new hardware
items.description: The Top 500 list records the fewest new entrants in its history amid a massive shift in compute infrastructure investments towards AI factories.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter China's LineShine remains the world's highest-performing supercomputer, according to the 68th edition of the Top500 list published at SC26 in Chicago on Monday. For the first time in decades, the supercomputer ranking saw exceptionally few additions despite unprecedented demand for high-performance computing hardware, as the vast amounts of compute resources deployed these days are destined for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers rather than traditional supercomputers.Top 10 supercomputers unchangedChina's LineShine, installed at the National Supercomputer Center in Shenzhen, offers sustained FP64 compute performance of 2.198 FP64 ExaFLOPS in the High Performance Linpack (HPL) benchmark at 42.22 MW. The machine relies on the homegrown LingKun platform with 304-core Armx9-based LX2 processors clocked at 1.55 GHz (13,789,440 cores in total) and the proprietary LingQi interconnect. Unlike the other four exascale-class supercomputers, LineShine does not use any compute accelerators and exclusively relies on CPUs, which is largely why it only gains 3.6X performance when moving from FP64 to mixed-precision data, which is lower than systems that use low-precision accelerators. (Image credit: Top 500)America's most powerful El Capitan supercomputer at the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory relies on AMD's Instinct MI300A accelerated processing units (APUs), and the HPE Cray EX255a platform delivers 1.809 FP64 ExaFLOPS at 29.69 MW, which makes it significantly more power-efficient than its rival from China. The Frontier supercomputer at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory, based on AMD's 3rd Generation EPYC processors and Instinct MI250X compute GPUs, achieves 1.353 FP64 ExaFLOPS at 24.61 MW. Meanwhile, Aurora at the Argonne National Laboratory, which uses Intel's Xeon CPU Max 9470 processors and Data Center GPU Max accelerators, offers 1.012 FP64 ExaFLOPS at 38.70 MW.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: All three American exascale supercomputers use HPE’s Cray EX platforms and Slingshot-11 interconnect.Germany’s Jupiter Booster at the Jülich Supercomputing Center, which employs Nvidia’s GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips, the BullSequana XH3000 platform, and Nvidia’s quad-rail InfiniBand NDR200 interconnect, delivers 1.0 FP64 ExaFLOPS at 15.79 MW and remains the most energy-efficient exascale supercomputer on the list. You may like AMD grabs over 40% of new TOP500 list for supercomputers, up 14% since last year The supercomputer race no longer means what it used to, as rankings lose relevance in the AI era Sanctioned Chinese supercomputer maker stripped of IO500 benchmark crown, Intel-powered Aurora retakes the lead Remarkably, neither the 10 highest-performing supercomputers nor the 10 most energy-efficient machines have changed their positions since June.Only 27 new supercomputers in Top 500 Only 27 new supercomputers (5.4% of all machines on the list) made it to the November edition of the Top 500, the lowest number since the project was founded in 1993. The most powerful newcomer is South Korea's Hanggang at the KISTI Supercomputing Center, which occupies the 12th position with 342.6 FP64 PFLOPS. The machine uses Nvidia's GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips and HPE's Cray EX254n platform. Hanggang also ranks eighth in the HPCG benchmark with 4.29 HPCG PFLOPS.The aggregate HPL performance of the world's 500 highest-performing supercomputers increased by a modest 4.4% over the past six months to 19.57 FP64 ExaFLOPS. Nonetheless, it now takes a machine with 2.857 PFLOPS of sustained FP64 performance to qualify for the TOP500, up 7.3% from 2.662 PFLOPS in June. The performance of the systems ranked 50th and 100th rose from 49.85 PFLOPS to 55.81 PFLOPS (12%) and from 21.85 PFLOPS to 22.74 PFLOPS, respectively. Also, there are now 27 machines that deliver at least 100 PFLOPS of FP64 performance, up from 25 in June, whereas the number of supercomputers equipped with compute accelerators increased from 275 to 291 (58.2%).Everything goes to AI data centers The historically low number of new entrants to the Top 500 is particularly noteworthy given the unprecedented scale of investments in advanced computing infrastructure these days. According to estimates by Epoch AI cited by the Top 500 authors, the amount of AI compute capacity added globally every quarter has increased by 2.5X per year. Essentially, the industry's priorities have shifted from construction of machines capable of solving exceptionally complex scientific problems to deployment of vast amounts of compute capacity for commercial AI workloads.In fact, the world's installed AI compute capacity already exceeds the equivalent of 15 million Nvidia H100 GPUs, according to Epoch AI. Furthermore, as of the fourth quarter of 2025, five major American hyperscalers accounted for an estimated 71% of the world's AI compute resources, much of which was deployed in massive clusters. While demand for advanced computing hardware is at an all-time high, it appears that the vast majority of new hardware never makes it to the world's most known supercomputer ranking. items.titleZh: 中国蝉联世界最快超算桂冠，AI数据中心吸纳新硬件
items.descriptionZh:
第68届TOP500榜单在芝加哥SC26大会上发布。榜单显示，中国“天河星逸”（LineShine）继续位居全球超算性能第一；但更值得关注的是，尽管高性能计算硬件需求处于历史高位，本次榜单新增系统却异常少，延续数十年的超算扩容节奏正被AI数据中心分流。大量新增算力不再进入传统超算排名，而是用于商业AI工作负载。

前十名与能效前十名自6月以来均未发生变化。部署于深圳国家超算中心的LineShine在HPL基准中实现2.198 EFLOPS的持续FP64性能，功耗42.22MW。该系统基于国产“灵坤”平台，采用基于Arm架构的LX2处理器，每颗304核、主频1.55GHz，总核数达13,789,440，并采用专有LingQi互连。与另外四台百亿亿次级超算不同，LineShine不使用计算加速器，完全依赖CPU，因此从FP64切换到混合精度时性能仅提升3.6倍，低于采用低精度加速器的系统。

美国最强超算El Capitan位于劳伦斯利弗莫尔国家实验室，采用AMD Instinct MI300A APU和HPE Cray EX255a平台，FP64性能1.809 EFLOPS，功耗29.69MW，能效明显优于LineShine。橡树岭国家实验室的Frontier基于AMD第三代EPYC处理器和Instinct MI250X GPU，实现1.353 EFLOPS，功耗24.61MW；阿贡国家实验室的Aurora采用英特尔Xeon CPU Max 9470和数据中心GPU Max加速器，实现1.012 EFLOPS，功耗38.70MW。三台美国百亿亿次级系统均采用HPE Cray EX平台和Slingshot-11互连。德国于利希超算中心的Jupiter Booster采用英伟达GH200 Grace Hopper超级芯片、BullSequana XH3000平台和英伟达四轨InfiniBand NDR200互连，实现1.0 EFLOPS，功耗15.79MW，仍是榜单中最节能的百亿亿次级超算。

本次榜单仅新增27台系统，占500台的5.4%，为1993年TOP500创立以来最低。最强新入榜系统是韩国KISTI超算中心的Hanggang，以342.6 PFLOPS位列第12，采用英伟达GH200和HPE Cray EX254n平台，并在HPCG基准中以4.29 PFLOPS排名第八。500台系统合计HPL性能为19.57 EFLOPS，半年仅增长4.4%；入围门槛升至2.857 PFLOPS，较6月的2.662 PFLOPS提高7.3%。第50名和第100名性能分别升至55.81 PFLOPS和22.74 PFLOPS，其中第50名增长12%。至少达到100 PFLOPS的系统由25台增至27台；配备计算加速器的系统由275台增至291台，占比58.2%。

新增系统稀少与AI投资热潮形成鲜明对比。TOP500援引Epoch AI的估算称，全球每季度新增AI算力容量正以每年约2.5倍的速度增长；全球已安装AI算力已超过1500万块英伟达H100 GPU的等效规模。截至2025年第四季度，美国五大超大规模云厂商估计占全球AI算力的71%，其中大量算力部署在大型集群中。这意味着产业优先级正从建造解决复杂科学问题的传统超算，转向为商业AI工作负载部署大规模算力。对超算生态而言，TOP500作为传统HPC性能排名，正越来越难以完整反映全球先进计算基础设施的真实建设方向；科学模拟、气候、材料等传统HPC应用可能面临与AI数据中心争夺芯片、电力和系统资源的压力，而能效、互连以及CPU与加速器路线选择仍将是系统设计的关键权衡。

items.title: New US rules aim to restrict Chinese firms’ remote access to AI servers and infrastructure
items.description: The Bureau of Industry and Security has announced a new interim final rule to ensure restrictions on the export of physical AI hardware cannot be bypassed by accessing it remotely in data centers around the world.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter New steps have been taken to ensure that countries and companies that are not on whitelists that would allow them to import advanced AI hardware cannot use cloud-based workarounds. The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has today unveiled an interim final rule, or IFR, in collaboration with the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council, aimed at backing up existing limitations on the export of hardware built by companies like Nvidia to non-whitelisted companies based in countries such as China. "The rule is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements" using data centers in third-party countries, a statement explains.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explainedNvidia, for example, is only allowed to export its high-performance AI chips to companies that are on a whitelist. But amid ongoing claims of black market GPU sales and a recent crackdown on overseas AI GPU rentals from China, it has become clear that these restrictions perhaps aren't as robust as they were intended to be. Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs were even recently discovered in a data center used by China Telecom.But while blocking the sale of physical goods is one thing, the cloud-based workaround is another entirely. Nvidia itself told data center operators earlier this month that they must limit remote access to their services — 51% of their business must come from non-Chinese companies. But, again, it's unclear how effective that approach has been in ensuring access to powerful AI capabilities doesn't fall into the wrong hands, even if they're accessed remotely rather than in person.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The new BIS rule means that overseas data centers will be required to do more to limit access to their services where U.S-based technology is being used. Restrictions will also be placed on data centers that supply remote access to companies whose headquarters are deemed to be in higher-risk countries, such as China, Russia, and Iran. A license will also be required for anyone trying to export advanced chips to companies with headquarters in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil. The new requirements will officially go into effect in 90 days.This latest rule comes against a backdrop of ongoing uncertainty over America's AI crown jewel, Nvidia. Jensen Huang, the company's CEO, resigned after confirming an affair, but is now potentially in line for a quick-fire comeback, despite the fact that the woman involved in the affair is an alleged Chinese spy. items.titleZh: 美国新规旨在限制中国企业远程访问AI服务器和基础设施
items.descriptionZh:
美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）会同财政部和国家安全委员会发布一项临时最终规则（IFR），旨在堵住非白名单国家/企业通过云端远程使用第三国数据中心、规避美国先进AI硬件出口限制的漏洞。此前，美国已限制英伟达等公司向中国等非白名单实体出口高性能AI芯片，但黑市GPU销售、中国相关方租用海外AI GPU算力等现象表明，仅控制实体硬件交付不足以防止受限制方获得先进AI能力。文章还提到，英伟达Blackwell Ultra B300 GPU曾出现在中国电信使用的一个数据中心中，进一步凸显规避风险。

从技术路径看，新规把出口管制从“硬件跨境销售”延伸到“远程计算安排”：非白名单实体不必直接购买芯片，而可通过第三国数据中心远程租用GPU算力或云服务，从而获得AI训练和推理能力。新规要求，使用美国技术的海外数据中心须采取更多措施限制服务访问；向总部位于中国、俄罗斯、伊朗等高风险国家的公司提供远程访问的数据中心将受到限制；向总部位于印度尼西亚、马来西亚、新加坡、泰国或巴西的公司出口先进芯片则需申请许可证。新规将在90天后正式生效。

合规阈值方面，原文未给出具体算力、带宽等性能参数，主要约束包括：英伟达此前已要求数据中心运营商限制远程访问，并规定其至少51%的业务须来自非中国公司；新规新增90天生效期、上述国别清单和许可证要求。其影响将覆盖云GPU租赁、AI算力服务、跨国数据中心以及AI模型训练/推理等场景，推动海外云服务商和托管数据中心加强客户审查与访问控制。执行难点在于远程用户身份识别、第三国子公司、云服务转租和算力访问溯源。文章末尾还提及英伟达面临持续不确定性，但未展开与规则直接相关的技术细节。

items.title: Researchers ‘recognize that AI will never replace HPC,’ says AMD executive — high-precision workloads will ‘exist for a very long time’ even as AI usage expands
items.description: The emergence of AI has seemingly posed a threat to high-precision FP64 computation, but AMD doesn't think the HPC world is moving away from those complex calculations in the wake of AI.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter While AI continues to reshape industries across science and mathematics, traditional supercomputing has seemingly taken a back seat. However, AMD's Scott Tease told Tom's Hardware Premium that most HPC sites “recognize that AI will never replace HPC,” and suggests that building a heterogeneous compute stack is the best path forward to tackle bleeding-edge research, despite Nvidia pushing performance on lower-precision data types higher for AI workloads at the cost of native performance for the important double-precision FP64 format that’s critical for HPC workloads.A heterogeneous compute stack brings together quantum, HPC, and AI under one roof, a fleet that AMD is helping pilot at Oak Ridge National Laboratory alongside IBM. Tease is AMD’s corporate vice president of HPC and sovereign AI, who joined the company earlier this year after more than a decade at Lenovo (and, before that, another 13 years at IBM). We spoke with Tease ahead of SC26 to get a read on the state of HPC, how it intersects with AI, and what’s actually driving the research community in a time when computer chips are driving headlines about international espionage plots.An awful lot of numbers (Image credit: AMD)FP64 is important for HPC workloads because of its precision. FP64 is a hot-button issue, largely due to how Nvidia’s GPUs have progressed over the past two generations. Or rather, how they haven't progressed. Nvidia’s latest Rubin GPU has 33 TFLOPs of FP64 compute, which is lower than the four-year-old H100’s 34 TFLOPs of FP64. For context, AMD’s year-old Instinct MI355X peaks at 78.6 TFLOPs of FP64 compute, while its upcoming HPC-angled MI430X peaks at 288 TFLOPs.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Nvidia has leaned on emulation to drive FP64 performance higher, a tactic that AMD is now pushing back on, but regardless, it’s easy to see why the HPC world could feel left behind in this new AI era. AI is defined by fuzzy, low-precision data formats, which is diametrically opposed to the accuracy of high-precision FP64. And, over the last generations of hardware from the big green giant that is Nvidia, FP64 performance has seemingly stalled in favor of driving low-precision data formats for AI workloads.“Maybe a few years ago, people in HPC might have felt a little threatened by AI because it was taking some of the limelight,” Tease told Tom’s Hardware Premium. “But I think now they’ve come to realize that AI is an essential part of scientific discovery today. It’s just, how are you going to deploy it?” You may like Anthropic says Claude Mythos Preview cut AMD MI355X onboarding from up to 12 months to around three days AMD VP and chief Zen architect rebuke claims that Nvidia and Arm made CPUs for agentic AI — ‘We didn’t magically know four years ago that agentic was going to be a thing’ The supercomputer race no longer means what it used to, as rankings lose relevance in the AI era That central question recontextualizes the apparent conflict between AI compute and HPC compute. Tease pointed to researchers spawning dozens of agents to explore viable paths for a given intent, while still leaving the complex simulations for a traditional FP64-driven HPC fleet. “...to try to do that with old approaches where you have islands of CPUs or islands of GPUs or something like that, and they're very different. They're not interconnected. It's just not going to be able to keep up,” Tease said.Enter quantum (Image credit: IBM)One of the challenges right now is actually connecting those systems, which is an area AMD is exploring with its recent collaboration with IBM and Oak Ridge National Laboratory to deploy AMD’s “classical” computing stack in the Umbra HPC system alongside IBM’s 129-qubit Quantum Nighthawk quantum computer. The systems will connect to the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility, allowing researchers to “explore how integrated quantum, AI, and scientific computing can accelerate scientific discoveries and national security.”If the HPC crowd felt slighted by AI, you can imagine how quantum researchers probably feel.Regardless, Tease says the future of scientific computing looks like a unified fleet that brings together AI, HPC, and quantum. “There [are] going to be a lot of problems where quantum will not be the be-all, end-all. There are some problems like human health, chemistry, where quantum’s going to allow us to do things we really can’t do with classical computing today. So having those things coexist, having them in a single workload, is where we want to get to.”Scheduling workloads for HPC is a solved game, with open-source schedulers like Slurm driving much of the TOP500 to properly schedule workloads on supercomputers. Tease described something that goes deeper to connect these systems. “What we want to be able to do is not only do those kinds of ‘where should it go, here or there’ for HPC, we want to figure out when AI could be applied to it, when [GPU acceleration is] appropriate… and also when is it best to go in a quantum environment?”The Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility is a test bed for figuring out how to hook these systems together properly. The press release explicitly states that it’s a “shared environment to evaluate the architectures, software, and workflows that future hybrid quantum systems will require.” The system is a co-design initiative with IBM, bringing together quantum and classical computing into one system.With the system, researchers are exploring how to accelerate quantum error correction with classical systems, a critical step in quantum computing to weed out environmental influences. The goal is ultimately to accelerate quantum systems in the Quantum Genesis Q competition, an initiative launched by the U.S. Department of Energy that will provide up to $215 million in funding for quantum research.By late 2028, the competition calls for quantum computers “with at least 100 logical qubits that are capable of performing hundreds of millions [of] fault-tolerant operations.” IBM describes the error correction research that will be performed at Oak Ridge as a “key component” in driving toward that goal. Separately, AMD announced last week an investment in quantum outfit PsiQuantum to provide CPUs, GPUs, and FPGAs to drive the company’s first fault-tolerant quantum system.

items.titleZh: AMD高管称，研究人员“认识到AI永远不会取代HPC”——即使AI使用不断扩大，高精度工作负载也将“长期存在”
items.descriptionZh:
在AI持续重塑科学与数学等行业的背景下，传统高性能计算（HPC）似乎一度退居次席，但AMD HPC与主权AI企业副总裁Scott Tease在接受Tom’s Hardware Premium采访时表示，大多数HPC站点已经认识到“AI永远不会取代HPC”。他认为，面向前沿研究的最佳路径是构建异构计算栈，把量子计算、HPC和AI整合到同一体系中，而不是让不同负载停留在彼此隔离的CPU或GPU孤岛。AMD正与IBM合作，在橡树岭国家实验室试点这一思路。

这一讨论的核心技术背景是FP64双精度浮点性能。FP64对HPC至关重要，因为科学模拟需要高精度数值计算；而AI负载通常使用低精度、较“模糊”的数据格式，以换取更高吞吐。文章指出，英伟达最新Rubin GPU的FP64算力为33 TFLOPs，低于四年前H100的34 TFLOPs；相比之下，AMD一年前推出的Instinct MI355X FP64峰值算力为78.6 TFLOPs，面向HPC的 upcoming MI430X更高达288 TFLOPs。英伟达近年更多依赖仿真来提升FP64表现，AMD对此持反对态度。这反映出AI时代低精度计算与HPC高精度需求之间的张力：英伟达为AI负载强化低精度数据类型，却在FP64原生性能上进展有限。

Tease的解释是，AI与HPC并非简单替代关系，而是科学发现流程中的互补环节。研究人员可以用数十个AI代理探索可能路径，再把复杂模拟交给以FP64为核心的传统HPC集群。旧有“CPU孤岛”或“GPU孤岛”彼此缺乏互连的方式难以跟上需求。异构计算栈的关键不只是用Slurm等调度器决定任务放在哪里，还要判断何时适合AI、何时需要GPU加速、何时应进入量子环境。这需要更深的系统连接和统一工作流。

在具体落地上，AMD与IBM、橡树岭国家实验室合作，在Umbra HPC系统中部署AMD“经典”计算栈，并与IBM的129量子比特Quantum Nighthawk量子计算机连接。该系统接入橡树岭领导计算设施（OLCF），作为共享环境评估未来混合量子系统所需的架构、软件和工作流。研究重点包括用经典系统加速量子纠错，这是量子计算剔除环境噪声、走向实用的关键步骤。应用场景涵盖人类健康、化学等经典计算难以处理的问题，也涉及国家安全。Tease强调，量子并非万能，但在部分问题上具有独特优势，目标是让量子、HPC和AI共存于单一工作负载。

这一合作也服务于美国能源部推出的Quantum Genesis Q竞赛：该计划将提供最高2.15亿美元资助，目标是到2028年底实现至少100个逻辑量子比特、能够执行数亿次容错操作的量子计算机。IBM称在橡树岭开展的纠错研究是实现该目标的“关键组成部分”。此外，AMD上周宣布投资量子公司PsiQuantum，为其首套容错量子系统提供CPU、GPU和FPGA。整体来看，AMD推动的异构计算栈意在把AI的探索能力、HPC的FP64精度和量子的特定优势结合，形成面向未来科学发现与国家安全的统一计算集群，并推动混合量子系统的架构、软件与工作流成熟。

items.content: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is once again addressing his controversial comments on PC RAM purchases. “I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM, I think everybody should be able to buy a lot of RAM for their own computer,” Altman said today. “I think the home tinkering is great.”The comments were made onstage at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World summit on Monday.Altman’s remarks on RAM stirred up controversy last month. In an appearance on the Cheeky Pint podcast, Altman said that it’s “quite terrible” for everyone to have RAM in personal computers rather than in data centers. He later followed up on those comments in posts on X earlier this month, saying, “i want you to have so much ram” and saying the original remarks had been “taken out of context.”AI companies have been buying up the world’s memory supply for data centers, leading to ongoing price hikes on everything from phones to game consoles. Altman commented on supply chain issues, saying OpenAI has “been constrained by different things at different times,” like memory, rack assembly, data center capacity, or “some random component.”Onstage today, Altman went on to say that “a few years ago we started saying the world needs to build a lot more memory supply chain in particular.” He acknowledged how RAM prices have soared over recent months, saying:“The world did not build out that much, and now we have seen DRAM prices — I don’t know exactly, but maybe they went up 5x, 7x, something like that. I think it would be much better if the world just had a lot of memory. That comment, which I think got misinterpreted, but there is a true part of it, which I will stand by is that, if we’re going to be in this memory supply shortage, then in some sense — whether or not we’ll decide to do it, because I think there are other tradeoffs like people having their own at-home inference — the optimal thing would be, can we share this memory and have it working 100 percent of the time rather than sometimes off in someone’s edge device? Again, optimal use of this limited supply. Maybe it’s not the reason to make the decision but that’s what I was trying to say.”Altman also commented on Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia’s CEO, saying he “doesn’t know enough” to say if Huang should be reinstated.

items.titleZh: 萨姆·奥特曼称他希望每个人都“拥有大量RAM”
items.descriptionZh:
OpenAI CEO萨姆·奥尔特曼再次回应其关于个人电脑内存采购的争议言论。他周一在Semafor主办的“硅谷与世界”峰会上表示：“我想说清楚，我希望人们拥有大量内存，我认为每个人都应该能为自己的电脑买很多内存。我觉得在家折腾硬件是件好事。”

争议源于奥尔特曼上月在Cheeky Pint播客中的表态。他当时称，让每个人的个人电脑都配内存、而不是把内存放在数据中心，是“相当糟糕的”。本月早些时候，他又在X上发文澄清，称“我希望你拥有非常多的内存”，并称此前的言论被“断章取义”。此次在峰会上，他再次试图解释自己的本意。

背景是，AI公司正在大量采购全球内存供应用于数据中心，导致从手机到游戏主机的各类产品价格持续上涨。奥尔特曼谈及供应链问题时说，OpenAI“在不同时期受到不同因素的制约”，例如内存、机架组装、数据中心容量或“某个随机组件”。他表示：“几年前我们就开始说，世界尤其需要建设更多的内存供应链。”

他承认近几个月RAM价格大幅上涨：“世界并没有建设出那么多产能，现在我们看到DRAM价格——我不确定具体数字，但可能涨了5倍、7倍，差不多这样。我认为如果世界上有大量内存，情况会好得多。”对于引发争议的言论，他解释称，其中确有他坚持的部分：如果世界将处于内存供应短缺，那么从某种意义上说，最优做法是共享这些内存并让其100%运行，而不是有时闲置在某个人的边缘设备中；当然，是否这样做还涉及人们拥有家庭推理等其他权衡，“也许这不是做决策的理由，但这就是我当时想表达的”。其核心逻辑是，在AI训练和推理对高带宽内存需求激增、供应受限的背景下，集中式数据中心内存的利用率通常高于分散的边缘设备，共享内存可提高有限资源的利用效率，但边缘本地推理在隐私、延迟和离线可用性方面仍有价值。

奥尔特曼还就英伟达CEO黄仁勋辞职的相关说法表示，自己“了解得不够”，无法判断黄仁勋是否应该复职。

items.title: Shareholders sue Intel, its CEO, and CFO after stock drops 28.6 percent in one day
items.description: The PC sales slump "more than offset” AI boom gains, shareholders say.
items.content: Intel is being sued by shareholders, who are accusing the chipmaker of misleading them about the impact of the PC sales slump that contributed to a drop of 28.6 percent in the price of Intel’s stock on October 30. The lawsuit (PDF), filed on Friday in the San Jose, California, federal court, is seeking class-action certification and lists the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System and “all others similarly situated” as plaintiffs. In addition to Intel, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan and Intel’s EVP and CFO David Zinsner are listed as defendants. The plaintiffs claim that Intel made “materially false and misleading statements and omissions” between July 23 and October 29. They are seeking unspecified compensatory damages, plus legal and other associated fees, for shareholders during that period. In the complaint, the shareholders argue that Intel misled them by failing to disclose: the full impact that the PC market sales slump would have on Intel’s third quarter and beyond; the impact of increasing PC component prices on PC sales for Intel’s OEM and distribution partners; that Intel was dealing with substrate supply constraints that would limit its ability to meet data center CPU demand; and “that any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset” by the PC sales slump. “[S]tatements regarding Intel’s business, operations, financial results, and ability to capitalize on the boom for AI-related infrastructure spending were materially false and misleading when made, and such statements did not accurately reflect Intel’s then-present business and prospects,” the law firm representing the plaintiffs, Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd LLP, said in a statement on Friday. On October 29, Intel announced what the complaint calls “disastrous” fiscal Q3 earnings. During the quarter, revenue for Intel’s Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) business declined 5 percent year over year. At the time, Tan pointed to an “unprecedented memory crunch” and manufacturing supply shortages hurting the PC market. The next day, Intel’s shares fell 28.6 percent in “the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years,” the complaint notes. Intel hasn’t publicly commented on the lawsuit.

items.titleZh: 英特尔股价单日下跌28.6%后，股东起诉该公司及其CEO和CFO
items.descriptionZh:
英特尔正面临股东集体诉讼。股东指控这家芯片制造商在2024年7月23日至10月29日期间，就个人电脑（PC）市场低迷对公司业务的影响作出“重大虚假和误导性陈述及遗漏”，导致英特尔股价在10月30日单日暴跌28.6%。诉讼于上周五提交至美国加州圣何塞联邦法院，寻求集体诉讼认证，原告包括Southfield市消防与警察退休系统及其他类似情况股东；被告除英特尔外，还包括英特尔CEO陈立武（Lip-Bu Tan）以及执行副总裁兼CFO David Zinsner。原告要求为相关期间股东索赔未具体说明金额的补偿性损害赔偿，并支付律师费及其他相关费用。

诉状称，英特尔未能向投资者充分披露多项关键风险：PC市场销售低迷对英特尔第三季度及以后业绩的完整影响；PC零部件价格上涨对英特尔OEM和分销伙伴PC销售的影响；英特尔正面临基板供应约束，这将限制其满足数据中心CPU需求的能力；以及数据中心建设和其他AI热潮因素对英特尔业务和财务业绩的正面影响，已被PC销售低迷“完全抵消甚至超过”。代表原告的律所Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd表示，英特尔关于其业务、运营、财务业绩以及把握AI相关基础设施支出热潮能力的陈述，在作出时存在重大虚假和误导性，并未准确反映公司当时的业务和前景。

案件背景是英特尔于10月29日公布被诉状称为“灾难性”的第三财季业绩。该季度英特尔客户端计算与物理AI集团（CCPG）营收同比下降5%。陈立武当时将PC市场受到的冲击归因于“前所未有的内存短缺”和制造供应短缺。诉状指出，次日英特尔股价下跌28.6%，创下该公司普通股50多年来最大单日跌幅。英特尔目前尚未公开置评该诉讼。

items.content: Constellation Energy – America’s largest operator of nuclear power plants – does not share Wall Street’s concerns that the Democrats will slow down data center development. On the company’s third-quarter earnings call last week, CEO Joe Dominguez was, for lack of a better word, unbothered as he addressed the blue wave.“I do think we’ve seen a bit of an overreaction in the market to the election results based upon fear that Democrats won’t let data centers get built,” Dominguez said.Many of the Democrats who seized control of the House and Senate in this month’s midterm elections ran on anti-data-center campaigns, which triggered a historic $2.5 trillion sell-off in AI-adjacent stocks that reached well beyond tech to the energy, construction, and materials sectors.Up until a few years ago, many of Constellation’s nuclear power plants were in severe financial distress and in danger of shutting down early. But the data center development boom and its enormous demand for electricity have dramatically reversed the nuclear industry’s fate.RelatedLame-duck Congress might actually do something: speed up energy projectsData centers lost the midtermsData centers want to suck everything dry — even the desertNow, Constellation and other companies like it are signing major deals with Big Tech companies to provide power to data centers. Microsoft, for instance, signed a deal with Constellation to fund the revival of a nuclear plant at Three Mile Island in Pennsylvania. (Three Mile Island is the site of what the Nuclear Regulatory Commission refers to as the “most serious accident in US commercial nuclear power plant operating history.”)Constellation also signed major contracts in the third quarter to provide power to Amazon and Google data centers, Dominguez said.Nuclear energy has had bipartisan support for years. The US Department of Energy classifies nuclear as a “clean” energy source because the act of operating a nuclear reactor does not directly produce carbon emissions. This makes nuclear an appealing investment to Big Tech companies that have to balance aggressive data center development with the ambitious climate goals they set long before the AI race took off. Still, nuclear energy has its issues. One of the biggest is nuclear waste, which the US government has not figured out how to dispose of at scale.Big Nuclear and Big Tech also tout these deals as good for the economy and job creation.“The market scare that people got last week was not lost on Democrats,” Dominguez said on the call. “They do not want to be the reason that the economy takes a nosedive by halting data center development.”Of course, Constellation’s future is essentially staked on the data center buildout, and Dominguez’s job is to convince investors they have nothing to worry about.In this instance, however, Dominguez really does seem genuinely unconcerned by the new Democratic majority in the federal government. It could be that he understands that, yes, while the Democrats won the midterms on promises of data center regulation and the blue wave included many new Democratic governors, data centers aren’t necessarily a strictly partisan issue. Some Democrats have opposed harsh measures like moratoriums — though on the flip slide, Constellation may also have to deal with challenges from the other side of the aisle.In Virginia, some of the state lawmakers who have been the most vocal about data centers are actually Republican. Virginia Sen. Richard Stuart, a conservative Republican, has aggressively pursued data center regulation. Last month, Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger, a Democrat, denied Stuart’s request for a special session to address a concerning new report from the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality on the state’s groundwater supply, which has become strained amid rampant data center growth.For years, companies like Constellation have been sitting on a bunch of old reactors teetering on the edge of extinction because they didn’t have enough customers to keep them afloat.The fight against data centers so far has been highly fragmented and hyperlocal, but that could change soon. The Trump administration loves data centers, and the federal government is working on wresting some control over data center development away from the states. But even then, Democrats and Republicans at the federal level tend to view data centers as an inevitable part of the future that needs some guardrails rather than out-of-control corporate growth infringing on the average American’s quality of life.Just look at the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, which was co-sponsored by two Democrats. The Senate is expected to vote on a passage of a sweeping bill which is being marketed as a way to speed up the permitting process for new power plants and transmission lines and connect new data centers to the grid faster. New Mexico Sen. Martin Heinrich, one of the Democrats backing the bill, has touted its inclusion of provisions designed to protect utility customers from rising rates due to data centers, ensuring Big Tech pays its fair share of costs. Researchers at Columbia University SIPA’s Center on Global Energy Policy called the bill’s protections “mixed,” noting they do not account for wholesale capacity and energy prices, a “principal way” data center electricity demand can lead to higher household bills.Senate Democrats are sharply divided on the bill, which critics say will fast-track data center projects at the expense of public input and environmental oversight and lead to a massive overbuild of energy projects that Americans will end up paying for.On Constellation’s earnings call, Dominguez pointed out that Virginia and Illinois, states with Democratic governors already in place before the election, have seen “a great deal of data center development.”“The bottom line is that Democrats care deeply about economic growth and they care very deeply about the many labor jobs that go with data center construction,” Dominguez said. “With labor such a key constituent for Democrats, it’s hard to imagine that we are going to halt work …There might be some differences and certainly there are going to be some local areas, I think, that are not going to want data centers.”Of course, Dominguez is speaking to investors here, and he wants to assuage their concerns. He also has a good point. Grassroots efforts to stop local data center development have been successful and have contributed to broader opposition to data center development across the country. But data center developers can also abandon projects and go elsewhere. Until a few years ago, data centers were largely concentrated in Northern Virginia, but with the AI boom, developers have fanned out across the country in search of available power and land. A total of 38 states have welcomed them with open arms and generous tax breaks, per the National Conference of State Legislatures.Of course, Dominguez is speaking to investors here, and he wants to assuage their concerns.Thanks to the convoluted way the US electric grid and energy markets work, Constellation’s power plants don’t even need to be located in the same state as their data center customers — the plant supplying the power just needs to be connected to the same region from which the grid is drawing power. The purchase agreement, in that sense, is symbolic: Because the data center needs more electricity than it can draw from the local grid without causing disruptions for everyone else, the data center pays for independent power providers like Constellation to supply the grid with extra electricity.That’s why data centers and the enormous amount of electricity Big Tech says it needs to power them have been such a boon for the nuclear industry. For years, companies like Constellation have been sitting on a bunch of old reactors teetering on the edge of extinction because they didn’t have enough customers to keep them afloat.Nuclear lobbyists will tell you that’s because the NRC’s safety regulations are overly restrictive and lead to untenable upfront capital costs that make projects impossible to finance. (This has been an industry talking point since 1979, after the NRC seriously overhauled its safety standards following the partial meltdown at Three Mile Island. That site is now owned by Constellation, which has signed a 20-year deal with Microsoft.)Both the Biden and Trump administrations have worked to support the development of nuclear power in the US by passing developer tax credits. The Trump administration has gone even further, pushing for a sweeping reform of the NRC that would make it much easier for new reactors to obtain operating licenses.And the Department of Energy this month approved a $5 billion loan to Constellation, which the company will use to upgrade its existing nuclear fleet. Another nuclear energy company, Vistra, received a $4.2 billion loan.It’s not totally unlike the Biden administration’s passage of the Civil Nuclear Credit Program in 2022, which planned to loan $6 billion to struggling nuclear companies in the US.That’s not lost on Dominguez.“Interestingly, in many respects the election had the Republicans saying a lot of the same things that the Democrats were saying,” Dominguez told investors on the call. “And I believe that the policy solutions are going to be somewhat similar.”

items.titleZh: 核电巨头不担心民主党叫停数据中心
items.descriptionZh:
美国最大核电站运营商Constellation Energy并未像华尔街那样担心民主党会放缓数据中心开发。公司首席执行官Joe Dominguez在第三季度财报电话会上表示，市场对中期选举结果的反应有些过度。中期选举中，许多民主党人凭借反数据中心竞选主张赢得众议院和参议院控制权，这引发AI相关股票历史性2.5万亿美元抛售，并波及科技、能源、建筑和材料等行业。Dominguez认为，民主党不会成为因停止数据中心开发而导致经济下滑的原因，因为民主党高度重视经济增长以及数据中心建设带来的大量建筑就业；他还指出，数据中心并非严格的党派议题，弗吉尼亚和伊利诺伊等民主党州长早已在任的州仍出现了大量数据中心开发。不过，地方层面的反对高度分散且确实有效，开发商也可能放弃项目转往其他州；在AI热潮推动下，数据中心已从过去主要集中在北弗吉尼亚扩散到全国，已有38个州以开放态度和税收优惠欢迎数据中心。

背景上，数据中心开发热潮及其巨大电力需求，已经戏剧性逆转了核工业的命运。几年前，Constellation许多核电站还处于严重财务困境，面临提前关闭风险；如今，该公司与大型科技公司签署重大供电协议：微软资助三哩岛核电站复兴，并签署20年协议；Constellation第三季度还与亚马逊和谷歌的数据中心签署供电合同。核能多年来获得两党支持，美国能源部将核能归类为“清洁”能源，因为运行核反应堆不直接产生碳排放，这使核能对需要平衡AI数据中心扩张与早先气候目标的大型科技公司具有吸引力。但核能仍有问题，最大问题之一是核废料，美国政府尚未找到规模化处置办法。

核心技术原理和商业模式上，核电通过核裂变产生热量、驱动汽轮机发电，作为基荷电源可以24小时稳定输出，适合AI数据中心连续高负荷用电需求；其运行不直接排碳，使数据中心可通过长期购电协议获得低碳电力支持。美国电网和能源市场按区域互联运行，Constellation的电厂不必与数据中心客户位于同一州，只需接入同一区域电网；购电协议在某种意义上具有象征性：数据中心新增用电超出本地电网可承受容量，于是支付独立发电商向电网注入额外电力，避免对其他用户造成扰动。这种长期购电协议为核电提供收入保障，甚至资助濒临关闭的机组重启，是核能商业模式的重要创新。但核废料处置、安全监管和前期资本成本仍是制约；核游说者称美国核管理委员会安全法规过严，导致项目融资困难，这一论点自1979年三哩岛事故后NRC大改安全标准以来长期存在。三哩岛是美国商业核电运行史上最严重事故地点，该站点现属Constellation，并与微软签有20年协议。

数据与政策支持方面，原文未披露具体装机容量或供电功率，主要披露交易和政策资金规模：AI相关股票抛售达2.5万亿美元；微软与Constellation签署20年三哩岛协议；第三季度与亚马逊、谷歌签署供电合同；美国能源部本月批准50亿美元贷款给Constellation升级现有核电机组，另一家核能公司Vistra获42亿美元贷款；拜登政府2022年民用核信用计划拟向困境核企提供60亿美元贷款；两届政府均推动开发者税收抵免，特朗普政府还推动NRC全面改革，使新反应堆更容易获得运营许可。与几年前财务困境对比，数据中心需求使核电从濒临关闭转为签约和升级。38州欢迎数据中心显示选址扩散，但地方水资源和环境压力上升，例如弗吉尼亚州环境质量部关于地下水供应紧张的报告引发关注，共和党参议员Richard Stuart积极推动数据中心监管并要求召开特别会议，民主党州长Abigail Spanberger拒绝了这一请求。

政治与监管上，联邦两党普遍将数据中心视为未来不可避免的一部分，但认为需要护栏，而不是任由企业增长侵蚀普通美国人生活质量。参议院预计表决《两党美国可负担性与就业法案》，该法案由两名民主党人共同发起，旨在加快新电厂和输电线路许可、让数据中心更快并网；新墨西哥州参议员Martin Heinrich称法案包含保护公用事业客户免受数据中心推高费率、确保大型科技公司支付公平份额的条款。但哥伦比亚大学SIPA全球能源政策中心研究人员评价这些保护“混合”，未计入批发容量和能源价格，而这正是数据中心电力需求推高家庭账单的主要途径。参议院民主党对该法案分歧明显，批评者担心它牺牲公众输入和环境监督、导致能源项目过度建设并由美国人买单。Dominguez则强调，民主党关心经济增长和建筑就业，地方可能有分歧，但不至于全面停工；他还称选举中共和党说了很多与民主党相同的话，政策解决方案会相似。总体看，核能因数据中心对低碳基荷电力的需求获得复兴窗口，但核废料、监管成本、地方反对、电网扩容和费率公平将决定这轮复兴的可持续性。

items.content: Fossil fuels are still the biggest source of electricity for hyperscale data centers in the US, a new paper published in the journal Nature Sustainability shows. They likely burn through more electricity collectively than many countries do, resulting in a serious amount of greenhouse gas emissions.The study homes in on hyperscale facilities — the massive structures spanning millions of square feet that developers are racing to build in large part to support generative AI. Researchers say the findings show that there’s a lot of work left to do to cut down pollution stemming from AI’s reliance on fossil fuels.“We tend to discuss AI’s environmental footprint as though it were some fixed property of the technology, when in reality the same computing infrastructure can have dramatically different consequences depending on the electricity system supporting it,” Gianluca Guidi, lead author of the new study and a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Biostatistics at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, says in an email to The Verge. “I actually find that encouraging, because it means these impacts aren’t inevitable. We have choices about where we build and how we power this infrastructure.”“The same computing infrastructure can have dramatically different consequences depending on the electricity system supporting it.”Guidi and his team used satellite imagery to identify 403 hyperscale data centers in the US, estimating each facility’s power consumption based on its electrical capacity. Using data from the Environmental Protection Agency, they approximated how much carbon pollution each data center would have produced if connected to the local power grid between May 2024 and April 2025.Altogether, the 403 hyperscale facilities likely consumed around 82 terawatt-hours of electricity that year, about 1.8 percent of all US electricity consumption. That’s even more than the amount of electricity that about 148 nations — a majority of the countries in the world including Austria, Israel, and Venezuela but excluding the largest economies including the US and China — individually burn through each year, according to John Sterman, director of the MIT System Dynamics group and MIT Sloan Sustainability Initiative.Electricity demand from these data centers produced 25.7 million metric tons of CO2 emissions, comparable to the annual carbon footprint of Denmark, according to the research paper. Sterman says that exceeds the total carbon emissions of about 113 nations. That’s because about 54 percent of the electricity the hyperscale facilities consumed likely came from gas and coal.Sterman, who was not involved in the research with Guidi, disclosed that he used the help of Claude to compare the paper’s findings to electricity use and emissions of countries. “I think AI can be extraordinarily helpful,” Sterman says. “But we’ve got to figure out a way to limit the harms … Especially because those impacts are irreversible. Once you allow these data centers to emit the CO2, you can never undo that.”Sterman says policymakers should require data center operators to bring new clean energy online. The study doesn’t account for local air pollution that can result from new gas infrastructure that’s being built to meet data center demand, or gas turbines that some AI companies have installed at their facilities to power themselves without connecting to the grid. And while hyperscale data centers encompass more than just AI-related computing, they also make up just a fraction of the thousands of data centers in the US — with more cropping up each year.RelatedThe global pledge to use AI for climate good is a cruel jokeThe study showed how big a difference the local electricity mix makes when it comes to the environmental impact of AI and data centers. Generating electricity in heavily coal-reliant Wyoming led to roughly seven times more carbon emissions per kilowatt-hour than in hydropower-rich Oregon. “Two data centers consuming exactly the same amount of electricity can have dramatically different carbon footprints simply because of where they’re located,” Guidi writes.Fengqi You, a professor in energy systems engineering at Cornell University who was also not involved in the study, says the results highlight the problem of “long-term carbon lock-in.” “Power plants and supporting infrastructure built to meet rapidly growing data center demand may operate for decades. Decisions made today could therefore shape emissions well into the future,” You says in an email to The Verge.Both You and Guidi also pointed out how problematic it is that researchers have to go through such great lengths to estimate energy consumption because data center operators won’t disclose that information. To that end, Guidi and his colleagues are using their research to build a website to track the environmental impact of individual data centers. A bipartisan bill making its way through Congress could also mandate greater disclosures nationally on data centers’ electricity use.“Communities and policymakers need reliable, independent data on what these facilities mean for our air, health, and the climate. This study is an important step.” Gina McCarthy, former White House national climate advisor and EPA administrator, said in a statement shared by the research authors.

items.titleZh: 美国数据中心如今的耗电量已超过一个中等规模国家
items.descriptionZh:
美国《自然·可持续性》期刊最新发表的一项研究显示，化石燃料仍是美国超大规模数据中心最主要的电力来源。随着生成式AI快速发展，开发商正竞相建设占地数百万平方英尺的超大规模数据中心，这类设施的单体规模和总体能耗远超传统数据中心。研究指出，403个美国超大规模数据中心在2024年5月至2025年4月间合计用电约82太瓦时，约占美国全国用电量的1.8%；这一用电量超过全球约148个国家各自的年用电量，包括奥地利、以色列和委内瑞拉等，但不包括美国、中国等最大经济体。相应二氧化碳排放约2570万吨，相当于丹麦的年碳足迹，并超过约113个国家的年度总排放。研究估计，这些数据中心约54%的电力来自天然气和煤炭。

在方法上，研究团队利用卫星影像识别出美国403个超大规模数据中心，并根据每个设施的电气容量估算其电力消耗，再结合美国环保署数据，按当地电网结构近似计算各数据中心在一年内的碳排放。该研究的创新之处在于绕开运营商普遍不披露详细能耗和排放数据的限制，以独立、逐设施的方式评估AI相关计算基础设施的环境影响。研究强调，AI的环境足迹并非技术本身的固定属性，同样规模的算力基础设施因所在地电力系统不同，可能产生截然不同的气候后果。例如，在高度依赖煤炭的怀俄明州，每千瓦时电力的碳排放约为水电资源丰富的俄勒冈州的7倍。也就是说，两个用电量完全相同的数据中心，仅因选址不同，碳足迹就可能差异巨大。

研究还揭示了“长期碳锁定”风险：为满足数据中心快速增长的电力需求而新建的发电厂和配套基础设施可能运行数十年，因此当前选址和供能决策将长期影响未来排放。研究未计入为满足数据中心需求新建天然气基础设施带来的局部空气污染，也未计入部分AI企业在设施内自建燃气轮机、不接入电网的情况。此外，超大规模数据中心只是美国数千个数据中心的一部分，且并非全部用于AI计算，但数量仍在逐年增加。

论文作者、哈佛大学陈曾熙公共卫生学院博士后Gianluca Guidi表示，这些影响并非不可避免，社会仍可选择在何处建设以及如何供能。麻省理工学院系统动力学组主任John Sterman指出，政策制定者应要求数据中心运营商新增清洁能源，而不能仅依赖现有电网。康奈尔大学能源系统工程教授Fengqi You也认为，研究凸显了长期碳锁定问题，今天的选择可能塑造未来数十年的排放路径。两位学者均批评数据中心运营商不披露能耗信息，迫使研究者通过间接方法估算。Guidi团队正基于该研究建设网站，以追踪单个数据中心的环境影响；美国国会一项两党法案也可能要求全国范围内加强数据中心用电披露。前白宫国家气候顾问、前环保署署长Gina McCarthy表示，社区和政策制定者需要可靠、独立的数据来了解这些设施对空气、健康和气候的影响，该研究是重要一步。整体来看，该研究提供了目前较为系统的美国超大规模数据中心能耗与碳排放画像，说明AI环境影响的關鍵不仅在于算力规模，更在于电力来源、选址和监管透明度。

items.content: Deb Shoquist leads operations at NVIDIA, overseeing the supply chain and manufacturing behind its AI platforms. That description sums up the job, but it doesn’t begin to encompass what Shoquist has made possible over decades. Shoquist, her team and their global network of manufacturing partners enable NVIDIA to introduce world-leading technologies year-round. Much of the team’s success comes down to her deep relationships with some of the world’s most accomplished manufacturers, including TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, SPIL, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Unimicron, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor. TSMC has partnered with NVIDIA since 1998. SPIL and KYEC were assembling and testing its chips more than two decades ago. For Shoquist, those relationships grow stronger through each challenge solved together on the factory floor, as every generation of technology demands more from the people and tools behind it. Ask her about the global network she relies on, and she starts with the people. There’s the supplier in Taiwan so eager to get production moving that he calls her at 3 a.m. with a fix to the latest problem. There are the factory workers in Vietnam whose only ask of her are more tools to get more work done. She remembers the partners that supported NVIDIA when it was small, and the work they’ve done to help each other grow. Shoquist meets with key suppliers quarterly and spends six weeks each year on the road visiting partners in Taiwan, China, Korea, Vietnam and the U.S., where conversations move from meeting rooms to factory floors. Recently, she paused her travels to accept the 2026 Dr. Lisa Su Woman of Innovation Award — and to share how she finds the right people and companies to imagine and produce at massive scale technology that has never been built before. Foxconn Q: How would you describe your job to someone outside NVIDIA? A: At the most basic level, our job is to convert designs into the physical world. Our design team creates a blueprint, and our job is to transition it into a reliable, high-performance supply chain. A matchmaker is probably the best analogy. You have to find the partner that matches your ramp style and has the technology that can meet the needs of very precise designs. The supplier has to be financially strong enough to invest in our ramps. They have to be highly technical. And they have to be willing to do something that has never been done before. If you don’t have all three, you can’t create products at the volume and speed that we need. You need those three legs, and in some cases, if you only have two, you have to invest in the company to make them a partner. Q: What’s an example of that in practice ? A: Amphenol’s cable cartridge is the most complex interconnect assembly they have ever built. When I recently visited the Vietnam factory, now in full production, I was struck by the level of precision required to build a product of this complexity. In this large cable cartridge, there are 1,500 small cable legs. Each one requires a very precise assembly to yield a quality level of less than 1 DPPM, or defect part per million. Amphenol built over a hundred automated lines to produce this product at the speed and scale we require. That takes know-how and technology, but it also takes heart, willingness and dedication. Creating anything of that complexity and precision with a supplier forges the partnership. The partners NVIDIA maintains are the ones who supported us when we were small, and yet are willing to scale with us today. Q: What changed as NVIDIA went from selling chips to building systems and platforms? A: When we were primarily a chip manufacturer, we were small, and the semiconductor industry was at scale. In that environment, it was about picking the best technology match for the products we envisioned. As we became a data center systems company, we needed more partners. But we’ve also now entered into new technology areas where the scale of the supply base is still developing. For example, our optical component partners have the technology and the willingness, but they don’t yet have the scale or capital to build fabs for the volume we need. To grow, we needed to support and invest, like we did with Coherent and Lumentum. Beyond that, with products like CPO (co-packaged optics), we’re creating entirely new supply chains with scale partners that are new to the optics world. Leading the integration of talent across the supply chain is the key to driving this incredible technology to high volume quickly. Wistron Q: You clearly enjoy spending time with supply partners, and in particular on the factory floor. What have you learned there over time that can’t be learned anywhere else? A: Over 20 years, you meet many individuals key to the success of your supply. You meet not only the CEOs, but also the people that are running the production floor. These are the people that really know the problems of manufacturing. If you don’t have a tight working relationship with the people deeper in the organization, then it’s hard to have an open dialogue about any challenges. But when you have tight relationships, they want to help you, and they feel comfortable enough telling you, “I need better technical support on the floor. I need more quality engineers. We need a better design. We need to automate this. We need more buffers of material.” That’s what 20 years of working with our suppliers has taught us. It’s year after year of learning from people, getting to know people deeper in the organization and creating the trust where they can tell us what we need to do to be successful with them. Q: Demand for NVIDIA technology is already massive and growing. Your job is to make sure NVIDIA’s volume can keep up. How do you make it happen? A: It goes back to relationships. When you decide that you’re going to push a line hard to increase volume, you have to have the relationships. You have to know their processes in detail. You have to know their people in detail, and they have to trust you. Only then are you in a position to ask them for special favors, because you can do it surgically, and your ask is credible and reasonable. And when you’re successful together, they’re happy, you’re happy, and the appreciation for the partnership deepens. We all appreciate those that make us successful. Coherent Q: How do you prioritize resources across the supply chain? A: You need to first understand what the most critical components are, and protect and prioritize production around them. We need wafers like we need air. And the critical component is the TSMC chip. As it comes out of assembly every week, we decide what factory gets what chip. Every week, we look at factory performance. If a particular factory yield is low, if their time of ownership is not at the level we want, they don’t get more chips that week. We keep track of every chip, from the identification number on the die all the way to the customer invoice. If you want to be our supplier, you have to support that traceability process. With that process, we took the time it takes from chip out at TSMC to system out at Foxconn and Wistron from five to two weeks when supply and demand requires it. Think of the supply chain as a large circulatory system with pathways everywhere — and when you need to accelerate any branch of it, you have the power to do that. We have the capability to do that. It’s empowering and exciting. Amphenol Q: What’s an example of a time things didn’t go as planned? How did you, the team and your partners find a way forward? A: We were getting ready to go to volume production with Foxconn and Wistron for the compute board of NVIDIA GB200. The last step in the process was a test managed by an automated handler — a completely new approach for us, developed to meet the demands of high-volume throughput for these complicated products. During the initial ramp, the throughput was significantly below plan. The operations director of Taiwan manufacturing made the call that to protect the product and shipments, he needed to disable the entire process and return to manual test loading. Our manufacturers backed him without question and brought in the necessary manpower to meet the immediate needs, literally hundreds of operators. That kept production moving, but would not solve the throughput requirement of full production. As with any operations problem, the root cause had many elements to it: test tray assembly, test tray design, automation hardware design, automation control software, product yield. From all viewpoints, it was a difficult problem to resolve quickly. That’s when we executed the NVIDIA swarm. Teams from NVIDIA design engineering, operations industrial, and product and test engineering, as well as from Foxconn automation engineering, flooded the line with talent to redesign and reactivate the line before the scale ramp hit. This is not an unusual occurrence when there is a problem in operations. All teams at NVIDIA are street fighters — action-oriented, and know no organizational boundaries. We say that “the mission is the boss,” but we also live “the mission is the boss.” Q: What makes this work so exciting for you? A: Operations is a very empowering place to be at NVIDIA. Our team is designing and implementing changes to the supply chain constantly to meet the strong demand of our new products. The challenges are understandably high, but we’re always given the resources we need to be successful. The only thing between our goals and our success is our own creativity. That is exhilarating.

items.titleZh: 全球最先进的AI基础设施供应链如何开创未来
items.descriptionZh:
NVIDIA运营负责人Deb Shoquist负责公司AI平台背后的供应链与制造体系，带领团队及全球制造伙伴将芯片和系统设计转化为可大规模量产的实体产品。她近期获得2026年“Dr. Lisa Su Woman of Innovation Award”，并借此介绍了NVIDIA如何在全球供应链中寻找伙伴、扩产并解决制造难题。NVIDIA与TSMC合作可追溯至1998年，SPIL、KYEC等伙伴也已合作二十多年；其关键伙伴还包括Foxconn、Wistron、Unimicron、Lumentum、Coherent、Amkor、Amphenol等。

文章的核心并非某一颗芯片的架构，而是NVIDIA在AI系统级产品时代形成的“运营创新”：把设计蓝图转化为可靠、高性能、可快速爬坡的供应链。Shoquist将运营团队比作“匹配者”，选择供应商需同时满足三点：技术能匹配高度精密的設計、财务实力足以支持NVIDIA的扩产投入、愿意做此前从未做过的事。若供应商只具备部分条件，NVIDIA会通过投资和深度协作将其培养为伙伴。这解释了NVIDIA为何在光器件、CPO等领域支持Coherent、Lumentum，并与新进入光学供应链的规模伙伴共同建设全新供应链。

在具体制造案例中，Amphenol为NVIDIA制造的线缆 cartridge 是其最复杂的互连组件之一，内含1500根小线缆腿，每根都需高精度装配，质量目标低于1 DPPM，即每百万件缺陷少于1件；Amphenol为此建设了100多条自动化产线，以满足速度和规模要求。另一个案例是GB200计算板的自动化测试环节：初期吞吐量显著低于计划，台湾制造运营负责人果断暂停自动化流程、恢复人工测试装载，数百名操作员保障出货；随后NVIDIA设计工程、运营工业工程、产品与测试工程以及Foxconn自动化团队组成“NVIDIA swarm”共同重设计并重启产线。这体现了其跨组织、行动导向的快速响应机制。

Shoquist还介绍了供应链管理方法：先识别最关键部件并优先保护，晶圆和TSMC芯片是核心；每周根据工厂良率、持有时间等表现分配芯片，并实现从晶圆裸片编号到客户发票的全流程追踪。借助该追溯与调度体系，在供需需要时，从TSMC芯片产出到Foxconn、Wistron系统出货的时间可由五周缩短至两周。她将供应链视为一个巨大的循环系统，可在需要时加速特定分支。

随着NVIDIA从芯片供应商转向数据中心系统和平台公司，运营复杂度显著上升：不仅需要更多伙伴，还要进入光学等供应链尚在成熟的领域，并推动CPO等新技术的大规模制造。其影响在于支撑NVIDIA AI平台全年持续推出和放量，保障GB200等复杂系统的高吞吐制造，并通过深度伙伴关系、投资、全流程追溯和跨团队协作，把前所未有复杂度的技术快速推向大规模数据中心应用。

items.content: Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 today, and the company is using the update to test new per device daily usage limits for some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features, according to MacRumors.Basic Siri commands and requests will remain free and unlimited, but more advanced features that rely on cloud-based processing like generating, cleaning up, or extending images in Photos will be subjected to the daily limits. There are four categories of limited usage, MacRumors reports, including using Siri AI for “multi-step, personal context requests,” image generation and editing tools, automations in Shortcuts that “rely on Apple Foundation Cloud and Cloud Pro Models,” and third-party apps that use those same cloud models.Apple hasn’t specified exactly how many times those features and tools can be used each day before limits are reached, but they’ll vary based on the task. The company reportedly plans to provide notifications when users are approaching their limit and have finally reached it.Instead of having to wait until midnight each day for your usage to reset, most of Apple’s existing iCloud Plus plans (excluding the 50GB option) will include higher daily limits at their same price. The $2.99/month 200GB subscription includes 2x the usage, the $9.99/month 2TB plan includes 5x the usage, while the $29.99/month 6TB and $59.99 12TB/month options bump the usage limit to 10x and 20x, respectively. Family members sharing an iCloud Plus subscription will have a shared usage pool that’s used on a first come, first served basis.Last week Apple updated Logic Pro with an option to “Buy More Usage” for that app’s intelligent assistant through $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs that are expected to be added to other Apple Creator Studio apps this month, including Pixelmator Pro, Final Cut Pro, Motion, plus Pages, Keynote, and Numbers.

items.titleZh: 苹果正在测试更复杂 Siri AI 交互的每日使用限制
items.descriptionZh:
Apple 在 iOS 27.3、iPadOS 27.3 和 macOS 27.3 测试版中开始测试针对部分 Siri AI 与 Apple Intelligence 功能的“每台设备每日使用限额”。基础 Siri 指令和请求仍免费且不限量；但依赖云端处理的高级功能将受每日配额限制，例如在“照片”中生成、清理或扩展图像。据 MacRumors 报道，受限场景分为四类：使用 Siri AI 处理“多步骤、个人上下文请求”；图像生成与编辑工具；依赖 Apple Foundation Cloud 和 Cloud Pro 模型的“快捷指令”自动化；以及调用同类云端模型的第三方应用。Apple 尚未公布每日具体可用次数，限额会因任务类型而异，并计划在用户接近和达到限额时发送通知。

在配额重置和付费方案上，用户不必等到每天午夜配额重置。多数现有 iCloud+ 方案（不含 50GB 档）在不涨价情况下提供更高每日限额：2.99 美元/月的 200GB 档为 2 倍用量，9.99 美元/月的 2TB 档为 5 倍，29.99 美元/月的 6TB 档为 10 倍，59.99 美元/月的 12TB 档为 20 倍。共享 iCloud+ 的家庭成员将共用一个用量池，按先到先得使用。除订阅外，Apple 上周还为 Logic Pro 的智能助手加入“购买更多用量”选项，通过 49.99 美元的 Intelligence Usage Packs 获得额外额度；该机制预计本月扩展到其他 Apple Creator Studio 应用，包括 Pixelmator Pro、Final Cut Pro、Motion，以及 Pages、Keynote 和 Numbers。

从技术逻辑看，这一调整体现 Apple 对云端 AI 推理成本的精细化管理：基础 Siri 保持免费不限量，以保障核心语音助手体验；而多步骤个人上下文理解、生成式图像编辑、快捷指令自动化和第三方模型调用等更复杂任务，需要消耗 Apple Foundation Cloud 与 Cloud Pro 模型算力，因此采用按设备、按日、按任务类型的配额。由于 Apple 未披露具体次数，现阶段无法直接比较各档位的绝对可用次数，只能确认 iCloud+ 档位越高，配额倍数越大，且付费包提供额外增量。其影响在于：一方面通过 iCloud+ 和用量包把高成本 AI 能力分层变现；另一方面家庭共享用量池可能带来先到先得的资源竞争，第三方开发者和重度创作者也需评估调用云端模型的使用成本。当前政策仍处于测试阶段，正式版限额和覆盖范围可能调整。

items.content: Nvidia’s board of directors “isn’t considering” having Jensen Huang return as CEO, according to a report from CNBC. A source tells the outlet the board “is focused on an investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back.”Since Huang’s resignation last week, tech executives, along with current and former Nvidia employees, have called for his reinstatement. An online petition to bring Huang back as CEO has amassed more than 180,000 signatures, including from major figures like Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, and Replit CEO Amjad Masad.RelatedThe Nvidia scandal isn’t slowing downPresident Donald Trump said on Monday that it “certainly isn’t a bad idea” for Huang to return to Nvidia. A report from the Financial Times also suggests that Huang floated the idea of returning as CEO with some of his colleagues.Nvidia appointed its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, as interim CEO. The company has also hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate Huang’s conduct.
