history.content: Deb Shoquist leads operations at NVIDIA, overseeing the supply chain and manufacturing behind its AI platforms. That description sums up the job, but it doesn’t begin to encompass what Shoquist has made possible over decades. Shoquist, her team and their global network of manufacturing partners enable NVIDIA to introduce world-leading technologies year-round. Much of the team’s success comes down to her deep relationships with some of the world’s most accomplished manufacturers, including TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, SPIL, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Unimicron, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor. TSMC has partnered with NVIDIA since 1998. SPIL and KYEC were assembling and testing its chips more than two decades ago. For Shoquist, those relationships grow stronger through each challenge solved together on the factory floor, as every generation of technology demands more from the people and tools behind it. Ask her about the global network she relies on, and she starts with the people. There’s the supplier in Taiwan so eager to get production moving that he calls her at 3 a.m. with a fix to the latest problem. There are the factory workers in Vietnam whose only ask of her are more tools to get more work done. She remembers the partners that supported NVIDIA when it was small, and the work they’ve done to help each other grow. Shoquist meets with key suppliers quarterly and spends six weeks each year on the road visiting partners in Taiwan, China, Korea, Vietnam and the U.S., where conversations move from meeting rooms to factory floors. Recently, she paused her travels to accept the 2026 Dr. Lisa Su Woman of Innovation Award — and to share how she finds the right people and companies to imagine and produce at massive scale technology that has never been built before. Foxconn Q: How would you describe your job to someone outside NVIDIA? A: At the most basic level, our job is to convert designs into the physical world. Our design team creates a blueprint, and our job is to transition it into a reliable, high-performance supply chain. A matchmaker is probably the best analogy. You have to find the partner that matches your ramp style and has the technology that can meet the needs of very precise designs. The supplier has to be financially strong enough to invest in our ramps. They have to be highly technical. And they have to be willing to do something that has never been done before. If you don’t have all three, you can’t create products at the volume and speed that we need. You need those three legs, and in some cases, if you only have two, you have to invest in the company to make them a partner. Q: What’s an example of that in practice ? A: Amphenol’s cable cartridge is the most complex interconnect assembly they have ever built. When I recently visited the Vietnam factory, now in full production, I was struck by the level of precision required to build a product of this complexity. In this large cable cartridge, there are 1,500 small cable legs. Each one requires a very precise assembly to yield a quality level of less than 1 DPPM, or defect part per million. Amphenol built over a hundred automated lines to produce this product at the speed and scale we require. That takes know-how and technology, but it also takes heart, willingness and dedication. Creating anything of that complexity and precision with a supplier forges the partnership. The partners NVIDIA maintains are the ones who supported us when we were small, and yet are willing to scale with us today. Q: What changed as NVIDIA went from selling chips to building systems and platforms? A: When we were primarily a chip manufacturer, we were small, and the semiconductor industry was at scale. In that environment, it was about picking the best technology match for the products we envisioned. As we became a data center systems company, we needed more partners. But we’ve also now entered into new technology areas where the scale of the supply base is still developing. For example, our optical component partners have the technology and the willingness, but they don’t yet have the scale or capital to build fabs for the volume we need. To grow, we needed to support and invest, like we did with Coherent and Lumentum. Beyond that, with products like CPO (co-packaged optics), we’re creating entirely new supply chains with scale partners that are new to the optics world. Leading the integration of talent across the supply chain is the key to driving this incredible technology to high volume quickly. Wistron Q: You clearly enjoy spending time with supply partners, and in particular on the factory floor. What have you learned there over time that can’t be learned anywhere else? A: Over 20 years, you meet many individuals key to the success of your supply. You meet not only the CEOs, but also the people that are running the production floor. These are the people that really know the problems of manufacturing. If you don’t have a tight working relationship with the people deeper in the organization, then it’s hard to have an open dialogue about any challenges. But when you have tight relationships, they want to help you, and they feel comfortable enough telling you, “I need better technical support on the floor. I need more quality engineers. We need a better design. We need to automate this. We need more buffers of material.” That’s what 20 years of working with our suppliers has taught us. It’s year after year of learning from people, getting to know people deeper in the organization and creating the trust where they can tell us what we need to do to be successful with them. Q: Demand for NVIDIA technology is already massive and growing. Your job is to make sure NVIDIA’s volume can keep up. How do you make it happen? A: It goes back to relationships. When you decide that you’re going to push a line hard to increase volume, you have to have the relationships. You have to know their processes in detail. You have to know their people in detail, and they have to trust you. Only then are you in a position to ask them for special favors, because you can do it surgically, and your ask is credible and reasonable. And when you’re successful together, they’re happy, you’re happy, and the appreciation for the partnership deepens. We all appreciate those that make us successful. Coherent Q: How do you prioritize resources across the supply chain? A: You need to first understand what the most critical components are, and protect and prioritize production around them. We need wafers like we need air. And the critical component is the TSMC chip. As it comes out of assembly every week, we decide what factory gets what chip. Every week, we look at factory performance. If a particular factory yield is low, if their time of ownership is not at the level we want, they don’t get more chips that week. We keep track of every chip, from the identification number on the die all the way to the customer invoice. If you want to be our supplier, you have to support that traceability process. With that process, we took the time it takes from chip out at TSMC to system out at Foxconn and Wistron from five to two weeks when supply and demand requires it. Think of the supply chain as a large circulatory system with pathways everywhere — and when you need to accelerate any branch of it, you have the power to do that. We have the capability to do that. It’s empowering and exciting. Amphenol Q: What’s an example of a time things didn’t go as planned? How did you, the team and your partners find a way forward? A: We were getting ready to go to volume production with Foxconn and Wistron for the compute board of NVIDIA GB200. The last step in the process was a test managed by an automated handler — a completely new approach for us, developed to meet the demands of high-volume throughput for these complicated products. During the initial ramp, the throughput was significantly below plan. The operations director of Taiwan manufacturing made the call that to protect the product and shipments, he needed to disable the entire process and return to manual test loading. Our manufacturers backed him without question and brought in the necessary manpower to meet the immediate needs, literally hundreds of operators. That kept production moving, but would not solve the throughput requirement of full production. As with any operations problem, the root cause had many elements to it: test tray assembly, test tray design, automation hardware design, automation control software, product yield. From all viewpoints, it was a difficult problem to resolve quickly. That’s when we executed the NVIDIA swarm. Teams from NVIDIA design engineering, operations industrial, and product and test engineering, as well as from Foxconn automation engineering, flooded the line with talent to redesign and reactivate the line before the scale ramp hit. This is not an unusual occurrence when there is a problem in operations. All teams at NVIDIA are street fighters — action-oriented, and know no organizational boundaries. We say that “the mission is the boss,” but we also live “the mission is the boss.” Q: What makes this work so exciting for you? A: Operations is a very empowering place to be at NVIDIA. Our team is designing and implementing changes to the supply chain constantly to meet the strong demand of our new products. The challenges are understandably high, but we’re always given the resources we need to be successful. The only thing between our goals and our success is our own creativity. That is exhilarating.
history.author: NVIDIA Writers
history.titleZh: 全球最先进的AI基础设施供应链如何开创未来
history.descriptionZh:
NVIDIA运营负责人Deb Shoquist负责公司AI平台背后的供应链与制造体系，带领团队及全球制造伙伴将芯片和系统设计转化为可大规模量产的实体产品。她近期获得2026年“Dr. Lisa Su Woman of Innovation Award”，并借此介绍了NVIDIA如何在全球供应链中寻找伙伴、扩产并解决制造难题。NVIDIA与TSMC合作可追溯至1998年，SPIL、KYEC等伙伴也已合作二十多年；其关键伙伴还包括Foxconn、Wistron、Unimicron、Lumentum、Coherent、Amkor、Amphenol等。

文章的核心并非某一颗芯片的架构，而是NVIDIA在AI系统级产品时代形成的“运营创新”：把设计蓝图转化为可靠、高性能、可快速爬坡的供应链。Shoquist将运营团队比作“匹配者”，选择供应商需同时满足三点：技术能匹配高度精密的設計、财务实力足以支持NVIDIA的扩产投入、愿意做此前从未做过的事。若供应商只具备部分条件，NVIDIA会通过投资和深度协作将其培养为伙伴。这解释了NVIDIA为何在光器件、CPO等领域支持Coherent、Lumentum，并与新进入光学供应链的规模伙伴共同建设全新供应链。

在具体制造案例中，Amphenol为NVIDIA制造的线缆 cartridge 是其最复杂的互连组件之一，内含1500根小线缆腿，每根都需高精度装配，质量目标低于1 DPPM，即每百万件缺陷少于1件；Amphenol为此建设了100多条自动化产线，以满足速度和规模要求。另一个案例是GB200计算板的自动化测试环节：初期吞吐量显著低于计划，台湾制造运营负责人果断暂停自动化流程、恢复人工测试装载，数百名操作员保障出货；随后NVIDIA设计工程、运营工业工程、产品与测试工程以及Foxconn自动化团队组成“NVIDIA swarm”共同重设计并重启产线。这体现了其跨组织、行动导向的快速响应机制。

Shoquist还介绍了供应链管理方法：先识别最关键部件并优先保护，晶圆和TSMC芯片是核心；每周根据工厂良率、持有时间等表现分配芯片，并实现从晶圆裸片编号到客户发票的全流程追踪。借助该追溯与调度体系，在供需需要时，从TSMC芯片产出到Foxconn、Wistron系统出货的时间可由五周缩短至两周。她将供应链视为一个巨大的循环系统，可在需要时加速特定分支。

随着NVIDIA从芯片供应商转向数据中心系统和平台公司，运营复杂度显著上升：不仅需要更多伙伴，还要进入光学等供应链尚在成熟的领域，并推动CPO等新技术的大规模制造。其影响在于支撑NVIDIA AI平台全年持续推出和放量，保障GB200等复杂系统的高吞吐制造，并通过深度伙伴关系、投资、全流程追溯和跨团队协作，把前所未有复杂度的技术快速推向大规模数据中心应用。

history.content: Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 today, and the company is using the update to test new per device daily usage limits for some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features, according to MacRumors.Basic Siri commands and requests will remain free and unlimited, but more advanced features that rely on cloud-based processing like generating, cleaning up, or extending images in Photos will be subjected to the daily limits. There are four categories of limited usage, MacRumors reports, including using Siri AI for “multi-step, personal context requests,” image generation and editing tools, automations in Shortcuts that “rely on Apple Foundation Cloud and Cloud Pro Models,” and third-party apps that use those same cloud models.Apple hasn’t specified exactly how many times those features and tools can be used each day before limits are reached, but they’ll vary based on the task. The company reportedly plans to provide notifications when users are approaching their limit and have finally reached it.Instead of having to wait until midnight each day for your usage to reset, most of Apple’s existing iCloud Plus plans (excluding the 50GB option) will include higher daily limits at their same price. The $2.99/month 200GB subscription includes 2x the usage, the $9.99/month 2TB plan includes 5x the usage, while the $29.99/month 6TB and $59.99 12TB/month options bump the usage limit to 10x and 20x, respectively. Family members sharing an iCloud Plus subscription will have a shared usage pool that’s used on a first come, first served basis.Last week Apple updated Logic Pro with an option to “Buy More Usage” for that app’s intelligent assistant through $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs that are expected to be added to other Apple Creator Studio apps this month, including Pixelmator Pro, Final Cut Pro, Motion, plus Pages, Keynote, and Numbers.

history.titleZh: 苹果正在测试更复杂 Siri AI 交互的每日使用限制
history.descriptionZh:
Apple 在 iOS 27.3、iPadOS 27.3 和 macOS 27.3 测试版中开始测试针对部分 Siri AI 与 Apple Intelligence 功能的“每台设备每日使用限额”。基础 Siri 指令和请求仍免费且不限量；但依赖云端处理的高级功能将受每日配额限制，例如在“照片”中生成、清理或扩展图像。据 MacRumors 报道，受限场景分为四类：使用 Siri AI 处理“多步骤、个人上下文请求”；图像生成与编辑工具；依赖 Apple Foundation Cloud 和 Cloud Pro 模型的“快捷指令”自动化；以及调用同类云端模型的第三方应用。Apple 尚未公布每日具体可用次数，限额会因任务类型而异，并计划在用户接近和达到限额时发送通知。

在配额重置和付费方案上，用户不必等到每天午夜配额重置。多数现有 iCloud+ 方案（不含 50GB 档）在不涨价情况下提供更高每日限额：2.99 美元/月的 200GB 档为 2 倍用量，9.99 美元/月的 2TB 档为 5 倍，29.99 美元/月的 6TB 档为 10 倍，59.99 美元/月的 12TB 档为 20 倍。共享 iCloud+ 的家庭成员将共用一个用量池，按先到先得使用。除订阅外，Apple 上周还为 Logic Pro 的智能助手加入“购买更多用量”选项，通过 49.99 美元的 Intelligence Usage Packs 获得额外额度；该机制预计本月扩展到其他 Apple Creator Studio 应用，包括 Pixelmator Pro、Final Cut Pro、Motion，以及 Pages、Keynote 和 Numbers。

从技术逻辑看，这一调整体现 Apple 对云端 AI 推理成本的精细化管理：基础 Siri 保持免费不限量，以保障核心语音助手体验；而多步骤个人上下文理解、生成式图像编辑、快捷指令自动化和第三方模型调用等更复杂任务，需要消耗 Apple Foundation Cloud 与 Cloud Pro 模型算力，因此采用按设备、按日、按任务类型的配额。由于 Apple 未披露具体次数，现阶段无法直接比较各档位的绝对可用次数，只能确认 iCloud+ 档位越高，配额倍数越大，且付费包提供额外增量。其影响在于：一方面通过 iCloud+ 和用量包把高成本 AI 能力分层变现；另一方面家庭共享用量池可能带来先到先得的资源竞争，第三方开发者和重度创作者也需评估调用云端模型的使用成本。当前政策仍处于测试阶段，正式版限额和覆盖范围可能调整。

history.content: Nvidia’s board of directors “isn’t considering” having Jensen Huang return as CEO, according to a report from CNBC. A source tells the outlet the board “is focused on an investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back.”Since Huang’s resignation last week, tech executives, along with current and former Nvidia employees, have called for his reinstatement. An online petition to bring Huang back as CEO has amassed more than 180,000 signatures, including from major figures like Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, and Replit CEO Amjad Masad.RelatedThe Nvidia scandal isn’t slowing downPresident Donald Trump said on Monday that it “certainly isn’t a bad idea” for Huang to return to Nvidia. A report from the Financial Times also suggests that Huang floated the idea of returning as CEO with some of his colleagues.Nvidia appointed its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, as interim CEO. The company has also hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate Huang’s conduct.

history.title: Intel bets on Classiq acquisition to turn Quantum efforts into commercially viable business
history.description: Intel aims to turn its quantum computing research effort into a commercial business by combining its silicon spin-qubit technology and manufacturing capabilities with Classiq’s established software platform and customer base.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter After having spent more than a decade pursuing quantum computing research, Intel is making its first real push at commercializing its efforts. First, with the pending acquisition of quantum computing company Classiq, which has an existing list of enterprise customers. Intel says it'll be the only company that can produce qubit chips and cryogenic control electronics at scale; the deal would give it a complete top-to-bottom hardware-to-software stack, and Intel will also gain the chance to become a leading vendor of quantum computing products. Intel's acquisition of Classiq is expected to complete in the first half of 2027.The key ingredient of that strategy is the pending acquisition of Classiq, which offers a hardware-agnostic quantum software development platform that enables engineers to design, synthesize, optimize, simulate, and execute quantum algorithms using high-level programming tools and AI-assisted automation, essentially untying software design from the complexity of quantum hardware. Meanwhile, Intel also plans to manufacture quantum processors using specialized versions of its 18A process technology, offer foundry services, and eventually sell complete quantum computers. Although the company expects its quantum business to become profitable, it acknowledges that commercial success will take time.Intel has spent more than a decade developing quantum computing technologies, including silicon spin-qubit processors, cryogenic control electronics, and software for hybrid quantum-classical computing. However, the company has largely treated these activities as research and development projects rather than an actual business. The acquisition of Classiq, which Intel expects to complete in the first half of 2027, marks a shift toward commercialization as Classiq already has many clients and established revenue streams.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: "Up until now […] our quantum computing group for the last ten years was […] purely a research and development project," said Pushkar Ranade, chief technology officer at Intel, during a media briefing. "It was not really viewed as a commercial activity."Intel's quantum hardware: The journey so farIntel's quantum computing journey kicked off in 2015 with a research collaboration with QuTech — the quantum research institute of TU Delft and TNO — to develop quantum computing technologies, including silicon spin qubits. The idea was to leverage Intel's extensive expertise in silicon transistor development and its high-volume semiconductor manufacturing infrastructure to produce quantum processors in the same fabs that make conventional CPUs, overcoming the manufacturing scalability challenges alternative quantum computing architectures faced at the time. Intel subsequently developed Horse Ridge, a cryogenic control SoC manufactured using a 22nm process technology in 2020. Three years later, the company introduced Tunnel Falls, a 12-qubit silicon spin processor manufactured on a 300mm wafer. You may like NEC has quietly quit quantum computing hardware development, report claims Intel shifts production capacity from consumer to server CPUs in face of 'unprecedented' AI demand Intel 14A moves closer to production as PDK 0.9 becomes available (Image credit: Intel)Intel's quantum computing effort focuses on silicon spin qubits, which use spin states of individual electrons to store and manipulate quantum information. The company chose this approach partly because silicon spin qubits can be manufactured using equipment and processes similar to those employed for conventional semiconductor devices. This compatibility enables Intel to re-use most of its existing manufacturing infrastructure and expertise rather than build dedicated semiconductor fabrication facilities for quantum processors that yet have to become commercial products.Despite the recent cuts at Intel, the company sustained its quantum computing project. Intel has developed two specialized versions of its 18A manufacturing technology for quantum computing: 18A-Q for silicon spin-qubit processors and 18A-CC for cryogenic control and readout electronics. To define/build 18A-Q, Intel has collaborated with Hitachi, AIST, and NEDO (three major supporters of quantum computing from Japan), and there appears to be a design kit intended to support large quantum computing systems. Without a doubt, 18A-Q and 18A-CC put Intel on the map of quantum computing chips in a big way. A couple of things should be kept in mind, though."The underlying device that we use, underlying process that we use to make the actual qubit device is a unique process, but it fits into those design rules," Ranade explained. "We can make these chips […] in the same fab that we use to make our CPUs."Although Intel 18AQ uses BEOL interconnect geometry and design rules derived from Intel 18A, its underlying qubit devices require a different manufacturing process. According to Ranade, the technology requires a specialized thin-film stack and several additional manufacturing tools. Nevertheless, more than 90% of the manufacturing equipment is identical to that used for conventional semiconductor production, according to Intel."Intel 18A-CC, meanwhile, uses 18A-based geometry but requires additional characterization for operation at cryogenic temperatures," Ranade said. "Crucially, Intel can manufacture quantum processors alongside conventional CPUs in existing semiconductor fabs, which could reduce the capital expenditure required to scale production. […] More than 90% of the process equipment is exactly the same." What to read next PsiQuantum turns its photonics know-how into an optical switch for supercharging AI data center GPU networks Quantum computing used in 'first commercial game development' Analyzing Intel's EMIB and Foveros advanced packaging roadmaps A major piece in the quantum computing puzzle: ClassiqFor conventional x86 architectures and IA-64 (while it was active), Intel has historically offered compilers that made software run better on its hardware (and sometimes on AMD hardware too). By contrast, with its quantum computing efforts, Intel has generally focused on hardware and while it has its own Quantum SDK that includes a compiler, this is not enough in the quantum computing realm as Classiq's offering operates at a higher abstraction level. With the acquisition of Classiq, the company intends to fill that gap. (Image credit: IBM)Classiq develops a hardware-agnostic quantum software platform that applies electronic design automation (EDA) principles to quantum programming, which lets developers design, synthesize, and optimize quantum algorithms without manually constructing circuits from individual quantum gates. The company's software provides high-level modeling, automated algorithm synthesis, optimization, debugging, and execution capabilities across different quantum computing architectures, which somewhat resembles Intel's approach to its x86 compilers, albeit working at a different level.Intel already has its Quantum SDK, which includes a C++-based compiler, runtime environment, and simulator for hybrid quantum-classical applications. Classiq's platform will sit above these tools and provide an application-development environment for programmers who lack extensive expertise in quantum computing.Intel compares the potential significance of Classiq's software layer to Microsoft's MS-DOS, which helped establish the personal computer software ecosystem; Nvidia's CUDA, which enabled developers to exploit GPUs for general-purpose accelerated computing; and EDA tools, which abstracted high-level design descriptions from the complexities of transistor-level integrated circuit implementation and essentially set the stage for the multi-billion foundry industry today.Furthermore, unlike Intel's quantum hardware business, Classiq already has commercial customers and generates revenue. The company employs approximately 130 people and serves more than 50 enterprise customers, including BMW, Comcast, Lufthansa, Rolls-Royce, and Toshiba. It also participates in more than 10 national quantum computing programs and supports over 50 quantum processors and simulators.As existing quantum processors remain insufficient for many practical applications, companies can develop and optimize software ahead of hardware availability. As a result, these customers primarily use Classiq products to develop quantum algorithms, train engineers, and create intellectual property in preparation for commercially useful quantum computers.Intel's CTO described Classiq's revenue and anticipated growth as healthy, but did not disclose actual financial figures."They have a very healthy revenue this year and a very healthy revenue CAGR over the coming years," Ranade said. "We hope that… we want that to continue."It is necessary to note that Intel intends to preserve Classiq's hardware-agnostic approach, which means allowing the company to continue supporting quantum processors and simulators from competing vendors. This is essential to maintain Classiq's existing customer relationships and expand its revenue opportunities, as its clients can/will be able to develop quantum applications without committing to a particular hardware architecture. Obviously, Intel can generate software revenue regardless of which quantum computing technologies ultimately become commercially successful."We very much want to maintain that hardware-agnostic platform that they have developed to attract more and more customers," Ranade said.From quantum chips to complete systemsWhen it comes to quantum computing, Intel's ambitions extend beyond manufacturing silicon spin-qubit processors. The company intends to become a supplier of complete quantum computing systems, which would combine quantum processors, cryogenic control electronics, classical computing resources, and software. For now, Intel has most of the building blocks required to develop complete quantum computing systems, but it still has to demonstrate that it can integrate them into commercially viable quantum computing at scale. (Image credit: Intel)"We want to be in the business of building quantum foundry components, but also complete quantum systems," said Pushkar Ranade, chief technology officer at Intel.Intel is also considering opportunities to provide quantum foundry services to other hardware developers. While its internal processor development will remain focused on silicon spin qubits, the company is open to manufacturing components for alternative quantum computing technologies, which somewhat resembles its approach to its x86 CPU and foundry businesses."We are committed to spin qubits," Ranade said. "But we are also open to providing foundry services to other modalities."Intel believes that its capabilities in photonics, advanced packaging, and semiconductor manufacturing could become commercially relevant even to companies developing quantum processors based on different physical principles than silicon qubits.Can quantum computing become profitable?Intel's decision to expand its quantum computing activities with the takeover of Classiq comes as chief executive Lip-Bu Tan emphasized profitability, financial discipline, and high-margin products across the company’s established businesses. Given that Intel's quantum computing initiative barely generates any revenue, let alone profits, the CEO stance raises questions about the viability of quantum computing for Intel, especially in a situation where the industry has yet to demonstrate widespread practical applications that justify the cost of large-scale quantum hardware. (Image credit: DNA TV/ FXP)When asked how Intel’s quantum computing strategy fits Tan's profitability requirements, Ranade explained that the company's immediate financial priorities primarily concern its established client and server processor businesses. Nevertheless, Intel must continue investing in emerging technologies that could shape future computing markets."This is really a bet on the future," Ranade said. "This is something we also have to do in addition to our mainstream businesses today."The Intel CTO acknowledged that quantum computing is not set to become a high-margin business in the near future. Meanwhile, the acquisition of Classiq gives Intel an established commercial software operation and revenue stream here and now, as well as an opportunity to expand customer relationships well before its own quantum processors reach commercial maturity. Intel also hopes that combining its hardware and software capabilities (probably including Classiq) will attract customers interested in complete quantum computing solutions.When asked whether vertical integration would make Intel's quantum computing operations profitable, Ranade acknowledged that he could not predict gross margins of the quantum computing business because the industry is still in its infancy. Nevertheless, he expressed confidence in the commercial prospects of Intel's quantum hardware and software."I expect it to become a profitable business very quickly on the hardware side, but too early to tell," Ranade said.Quantum computing will remain hybridEven though quantum processors evolve at a rapid pace, the technology is unlikely to replace existing CPUs and GPUs for conventional computing any time soon. Instead, Intel expects quantum computing systems to operate alongside the usual processors in data centers and supercomputing environments. (Image credit: Institute for Molecular Science) (Image credit: David Awschalom / University of Chicago)Classiq's software platform will provide high-level quantum algorithm development capabilities, while Intel Quantum SDK will handle compilation, simulation, and hybrid quantum-classical execution. This approach differs from Nvidia's CUDA-Q, which is designed to integrate quantum computing workflows with existing accelerated computing infrastructure. According to Classiq chief executive Nir Minerbi, Classiq operates at a higher level of abstraction and can complement CUDA-Q rather than compete with it."CUDA Q is very much low-level; it is gate-level. It is a good platform, by the way, but it is very low-level," said Minerbi. "The reason companies like Rolls-Royce and BMW and others use the Classiq platform on top of CUDA Q is due to the level of abstraction. It is much, much easier to develop quantum programs with Classiq and then to simulate it with CUDA Q rather than only with CUDA Q."Meanwhile, commercial success of quantum computing still depends on substantial advances in quantum hardware, including qubit scalability, error correction, control electronics, and system integration. For now, many Classiq customers are developing applications for quantum computers that have yet to reach the scale required for commercially valuable workloads.SummaryIntel expects to complete its acquisition of Classiq in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. The company has not disclosed the purchase price or other financial terms.The transaction will bring Classiq's software development capabilities and established customer relationships into Intel's quantum computing organization, but will preserve the platform's compatibility with competing hardware technologies. For Intel, the acquisition represents an opportunity to turn more than a decade of quantum computing research into a commercial business unit as it will have all the building blocks required to create quantum systems. Furthermore, Intel's quantum computing business will be open to third parties in the sense that Intel will be able to build quantum processors for partners using its 18AQ and 18ACC process technologies.Whether Intel's quantum computing business eventually delivers the high margins Intel seeks will depend not only on Intel's ability to build systems, produce quantum chips for others, or Classiq's software revenue, but also on the industry's ability to develop quantum processors and systems capable of solving real-world problems that people are willing to pay for.
history.author: Anton Shilov
history.titleZh: 英特尔押注收购Classiq，以将其量子业务打造成具备商业可行性的业务
history.descriptionZh:
英特尔在经历十余年量子计算研究后，正首次实质性推动该业务商业化。核心动作是收购量子软件公司Classiq，交易预计在2027年上半年完成，仍需监管批准，收购金额未披露。Classiq已拥有企业客户和收入来源。英特尔称，交易完成后将具备从量子比特芯片、低温控制电子到软件栈的完整能力，并成为能够规模化生产量子比特芯片和低温控制电子、进而提供完整量子计算系统的厂商。英特尔计划用18A工艺的专用版本制造量子处理器、提供量子代工服务，并最终销售完整量子计算机；同时承认量子业务实现商业成功仍需时间。

背景方面，英特尔自2015年起与QuTech（代尔夫特理工大学与TNO的量子研究机构）合作开发硅自旋量子比特等技术，希望复用其在硅晶体管和高量产晶圆制造上的经验，在现有CPU晶圆厂中生产量子处理器，以解决其他量子架构面临的制造扩展难题。2020年，英特尔推出22nm工艺制造的Horse Ridge低温控制SoC；2023年推出在300mm晶圆上制造的12量子比特硅自旋量子比特处理器Tunnel Falls。尽管公司近期有裁员和成本削减，量子项目仍得以维持。英特尔的技术路线核心是硅自旋量子比特，即利用单个电子的自旋态存储和操纵量子信息，其优势是与传统半导体设备和工艺高度兼容，可复用大部分现有制造基础设施。

在制造技术上，英特尔为量子计算开发了两个18A衍生版本：18A-Q用于硅自旋量子比特处理器，18A-CC用于低温控制与读取电子。18A-Q沿用英特尔18A的后段互连几何与设计规则，但量子比特器件需要特殊薄膜叠层和额外制造工具；英特尔称超过90%的制造设备与常规半导体生产相同。18A-CC基于18A几何，但需要针对低温运行进行额外表征。关键之处在于，英特尔可在现有晶圆厂中把量子处理器与常规CPU并行制造，从而降低扩大产能所需的资本开支。英特尔还与日立、AIST、NEDO合作定义18A-Q，并似乎已有面向大型量子系统的设计套件。

Classiq是此次商业化的关键软件拼图。其平台是硬件无关的量子软件开发平台，把电子设计自动化（EDA）原则引入量子编程，让工程师通过高层编程工具和AI辅助自动化来设计、综合、优化、模拟和执行量子算法，而不必手工从单个量子门搭建电路。平台提供高层建模、自动算法综合、优化、调试及跨架构执行能力，位于英特尔Quantum SDK之上；后者包含基于C++的编译器、运行时和混合量子-经典模拟器。英特尔将Classiq软件层的潜在意义类比为微软MS-DOS对PC软件生态、NVIDIA CUDA对通用GPU计算、EDA工具对集成电路和代工产业的作用。Classiq约有130名员工，服务50多家企业客户，包括宝马、康卡斯特、汉莎、罗尔斯·罗伊斯和东芝，参与10多个国家量子项目，支持50多种量子处理器和模拟器。其已有商业收入和健康增长，但英特尔未披露具体财务数据。

英特尔表示将保留Classiq的硬件无关路线，允许其继续支持竞争对手的量子处理器和模拟器。这有助于维持客户关系并扩大软件收入，也使英特尔无论哪种量子硬件路线最终胜出都能获得软件收益。Classiq CEO称，其抽象层次高于NVIDIA CUDA-Q；CUDA-Q偏底层、门级，而Classiq可在CUDA-Q之上使用，宝马、罗尔斯·罗伊斯等客户正是用Classiq开发量子程序，再用CUDA-Q模拟，二者互补而非直接竞争。

英特尔的目标不止于芯片，还包括完整量子计算系统，即整合量子处理器、低温控制电子、经典计算资源和软件。公司内部处理器研发仍聚焦硅自旋量子比特，但对为其他量子模态提供代工服务持开放态度，并认为其在光子学、先进封装和半导体制造方面的能力对采用不同物理原理的量子处理器开发商也有商业价值。英特尔预计量子计算将长期以混合模式存在，不会很快取代CPU和GPU，而是与经典处理器一起用于数据中心和超算环境。Classiq负责高层算法开发，英特尔Quantum SDK负责编译、模拟和混合执行。

财务上，英特尔CEO陈立武强调盈利、财务纪律和高毛利产品，而量子业务目前几乎不贡献收入，更谈不上利润。英特尔CTO Pushkar Ranade称，这是对未来下注，主流客户端和服务器处理器仍是当前财务优先项；量子计算短期内不会成为高毛利业务，收购Classiq可立即带来软件收入、客户关系和交叉销售机会。他无法预测量子业务毛利率，但预计硬件侧会较快成为盈利业务，不过为时过早。最终，英特尔量子业务能否带来高利润，不仅取决于其系统集成、量子芯片代工和Classiq软件收入，还取决于整个行业能否在量子比特扩展、纠错、控制电子、系统集成以及可付费的真实应用上取得实质突破。

history.title: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics
history.description: To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient. Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering […]
history.content: To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient. Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale. “Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.” Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics. Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity. In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute. NVIDIA Photonics addresses both power efficiency and resiliency. By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics. It also uses 4x fewer lasers, which means fewer components that can fail. Cooler Optics, Replaceable Light Sources Increase Resiliency Lambda’s deployment uses NVIDIA Photonics switches, each with 144 ports running at 800Gb/s. Liquid cooling carries heat away from the switch chip and optical engines. The company reports a median optics temperature of 36°C, compared with 51°C for conventional pluggable optics, and its tests find more stable signal integrity. NVIDIA Photonics also brings the electrical-to-optical conversion closer to the switch chip. Each switch has 18 removable external light sources, which supply light to the optical engines. Optical engines sit alongside the chip on the same package and convert electrical signals into light that carries data over fiber between parts of the cluster. Technicians can replace the light-source modules in the field, unlike traditional pluggable optics, which require replacing the entire module if a laser fails. Co-packaging shortens the electrical path from inches to millimeters, which reduces signal loss. It also removes the need for retimer chips, cutting both power draw and the number of parts in the signal path. Explore NVIDIA Photonics and read Lambda’s deployment announcement. history.titleZh: Lambda 借助 NVIDIA Photonics 提升 AI 工厂的韧性与效率
history.descriptionZh:
Lambda 正在采用 NVIDIA Photonics 共封装光学（CPO）交换机，为其大规模 AI 工厂构建高速、高效且高可靠的网络。背景是：训练 AI 模型需要数千块 GPU 协同工作，网络必须跟上越来越大的 AI 集群需求。Lambda 将用这些交换机连接 NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 机架，支持超过 10,000 块 GPU 的部署。Lambda 云服务总裁 Dave Ward 表示，把共封装光学引入这一规模的部署，是构建下一代 AI 所需基础设施的重要一步。

技术原理上，NVIDIA Photonics 用位于交换机封装上的共封装光学引擎替代传统可插拔光模块，使电信号到光信号的转换更靠近交换芯片。光学引擎与芯片位于同一封装内，负责把电信号转换为光信号，并通过光纤在集群各部分之间传输数据。共封装把电连接路径从英寸级缩短到毫米级，从而减少信号损耗，并移除重定时器（retimer）芯片，降低功耗和信号路径中的部件数量。每台交换机有 144 个 800Gb/s 端口，并配有 18 个可移除的外部光源模块，为光学引擎供光。由于光源模块可在现场更换，而传统可插拔光学模块在激光器故障时通常需要更换整个模块，因此这种设计提升了可维护性和可靠性。Lambda 的部署还采用液冷，将交换芯片和光学引擎的热量带走。

性能参数方面，Lambda 的测试显示，使用这些交换机后，机架级网络延迟降低约 4%，pod 级最高降低约 10%；在机架、可扩展单元和 pod 配置中，网络吞吐与传统可插拔光学方案相同。NVIDIA Photonics 相比传统可插拔光学，能效最高提升 5 倍，可靠性最高提升 15 倍，并减少 4 倍激光器数量，从而减少可能故障的组件。Lambda 报告其光学模块温度中位数为 36°C，而传统可插拔光学为 51°C，测试还发现信号完整性更稳定。

技术影响和应用场景方面，网络位于 AI 工厂生产力的核心：在大规模训练任务中，一条链路中断可能拖住数千块 GPU；在代理式推理中，一次网络中断可能对多个代理产生级联延迟效应。每次中断都意味着时间损失，而网络消耗的每一瓦功耗都意味着可用于计算的功耗减少。因此，CPO 交换机通过降低功耗、提高可靠性和延长平均无中断时间，有助于减少大规模 AI 集群的停机风险，提升训练和推理效率，并降低运维复杂度。该方案适用于超大规模 GPU 集群、AI 训练工厂和代理式推理等对网络带宽、能效与韧性要求极高的场景。

history.title: NVIDIA Expands Slurm to Bring Quantum Computing Into Supercomputing
history.description: Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors.  Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows […]
history.content: Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors. Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows and tools, enabling computational chemists, nuclear physicists and materials scientists to bring quantum computing into their research domains without friction. In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. This makes it easier than ever for HPC centers and QPU builders to integrate and serve their hardware. The expansion is already being adopted by Alice & Bob, IBM, IQM, Pasqal, Quantinuum and MQSC and supports the widely used QRMI and QDMI interfaces. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Beating the Bottleneck Until now, integrating a QPU into a supercomputing center meant a new software challenge for every new QPU or supercomputing center. By building on existing quantum-HPC interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI, the Slurm expansion allows QPU builders to reuse their integrations across all their deployments. It also means that supercomputing centers can add new quantum processors to their existing scheduling and resource-management workflows without developing bespoke QPU-specific solutions. For quantum computing to advance science, it needs to be used by scientists. Now scientists can run quantum-classical applications developed with platforms such as NVIDIA CUDA-Q with Slurm coordinating access to all the processing they need. Slurm 26.11 will be available later this month. Orchestrating Resources in an Open Quantum-GPU Platform The Slurm expansion adds a community-developed orchestration layer to NVIDIA’s open platform for quantum-GPU supercomputing, which centers around the CUDA-Q open platform for hybrid quantum-classical computing. At SC26, new releases expand all aspects of the platform: CUDA-Q QEC allows researchers developing quantum error correction to rapidly prototype and test new ideas, including with a new decoder server. A new TCBP-JOBS decoder is 13,000x faster than the industry standard. CUDA-Q gets an expanded layer of fault-tolerant primitives that application builders can use to realistically compile their ideas. Fermilab has already used CUDA-Q to perform studies in three weeks that would normally have taken five months. CUDA-Q Algorithms provides reusable components for builders of quantum applications, including new capabilities in helping design the loading data into quantum circuits and tools specifically for chemistry and materials applications CUDA-Q Pulse gives quantum hardware builders a layer for shaping the ‘pulses’ needed to control qubits on a QPU, including tools to GPU accelerate their generation. The quantum ecosystem around the world is continuing to build with this platform. Quantum Motion integrated its QUICHE chemistry framework with CUDA-Q. Altera and Oxford Quantum Circuits designed an FPGA-based controller connecting qubit control and readout to GPUs through NVQLink. At supercomputing scale, QunaSys used cuQuantum and 1,024 NVIDIA Hopper GPUs on ABCI-Q to simulate more than 300 million quantum operations, reaching chemical accuracy for a four-hydrogen-atom model. NVIDIA researchers used JUPITER to simulate 104 qubits under realistic noise, testing fault-tolerant designs before they’re built. Learn more about NVIDIA quantum computing technologies. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26

history.titleZh: 英伟达扩展 Slurm，将量子计算引入超级计算
history.descriptionZh:
过去五年，超级计算中心中的量子处理器部署量增长近七倍。目前全球近30个超算中心正在部署超过50台量子处理器。许多超算中心使用Slurm运行科学超算工作负载，因此扩展Slurm对量子处理器的支持，可以建立在科研人员熟悉的流程和工具之上，使计算化学家、核物理学家和材料科学家无需额外适配即可将量子计算引入研究领域。在新版本中，Slurm基于此前与IBM、Pasqal及更广泛量子计算社区的合作，允许量子处理器（QPU）厂商通过一个简单文件，为其硬件面向所有超算中心创建统一接口。这使高性能计算（HPC）中心和QPU厂商更容易集成并对外提供硬件服务。该扩展已被Alice & Bob、IBM、IQM、Pasqal、Quantinuum和MQSC采用，并支持广泛使用的QRMI和QDMI接口。

此前，将QPU集成到超算中心意味着每新增一台QPU或一个超算中心，都要面对新的软件开发挑战。Slurm此次扩展通过复用QRMI、QDMI等已有量子-HPC接口，使QPU厂商能够在所有部署中复用其集成工作；超算中心也可以把新的量子处理器加入现有调度和资源管理工作流，而无需开发针对特定QPU的定制方案。这对量子计算推动科学进步至关重要，因为量子计算需要被科学家实际使用。现在，科学家可以通过Slurm协调所需全部处理资源，运行使用NVIDIA CUDA-Q等平台开发的量子-经典混合应用。Slurm 26.11将于本月晚些时候发布。

这一Slurm扩展为NVIDIA开放量子-GPU超算平台增加了社区开发的编排层，该平台以面向混合量子-经典计算的CUDA-Q开放平台为核心。在SC26上，新版本扩展了平台各个方面：CUDA-Q QEC让量子纠错研究人员能够快速原型设计和测试新想法，包括新的解码器服务器；新的TCBP-JOBS解码器比行业标准快13,000倍。CUDA-Q增加了扩展的容错原语层，应用构建者可用其更贴近实际地编译想法。Fermilab已使用CUDA-Q在三周内完成通常需要五个月的研究。CUDA-Q Algorithms为量子应用构建者提供可复用组件，包括帮助设计将数据加载到量子电路的新能力，以及面向化学和材料应用的专用工具。CUDA-Q Pulse为量子硬件构建者提供塑造控制QPU量子比特所需“脉冲”的层，包括用GPU加速脉冲生成的工具。

全球量子生态正在该平台上持续构建。Quantum Motion将其QUICHE化学框架与CUDA-Q集成；Altera和Oxford Quantum Circuits设计了基于FPGA的控制器，通过NVQLink将量子比特控制与读出连接到GPU。在超算规模上，QunaSys使用cuQuantum和ABCI-Q上的1,024块NVIDIA Hopper GPU模拟了超过3亿次量子操作，并在四氢原子模型上达到化学精度。NVIDIA研究人员使用JUPITER在真实噪声条件下模拟104个量子比特，在容错设计实际构建前对其进行测试。总体来看，Slurm对量子处理器的原生支持降低了量子硬件与HPC调度系统的集成门槛，而CUDA-Q生态的扩展则覆盖纠错、容错编译、算法组件、脉冲控制和GPU加速模拟等关键环节，推动量子-经典混合计算从实验探索走向超算中心的实际科研工作流。
